# viveEditor · Documentation

> viveEditor documentation: installing, frameworks, the toolbar, images, video, tables, Word and Markdown, server-side cleaning, Laravel and extras.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/

---

# Installation

> Add viveEditor with one CDN script or from npm, pick the packages you need and load the right stylesheets.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

You can add viveEditor to a page with one script from a CDN, or install it from npm and build it with your bundler. This page shows both ways, which packages to choose and which stylesheets to load.

## With a CDN script

This needs no build step. Load the stylesheet and the script, then mark a textarea with `data-editor`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/viveeditor@x.y.z/dist/viveeditor.css" />
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/viveeditor@x.y.z/dist/viveeditor.classic.iife.js"></script>

<form method="post">
  <label for="body">Article</label>
  <textarea id="body" name="body" data-editor required></textarea>
</form>
```

Replace `x.y.z` with the exact version you use. When the page is ready, the script turns every `textarea[data-editor]` into an editor with the toolbar and exposes `window.ViveEditor`. The form posts clean HTML under the textarea's name. Always sanitize it again on the server.

The script carries basic formatting, lists, alignment and colours, checklists, code blocks (without syntax colouring), tables, find and replace, images (by address, no uploader), video embeds and clean paste from Office. Mentions, emoji, formulas, footnotes, templates and the AI assistant are npm only, and so is the `<vive-editor>` element.

> **Keep the exact version and the file names**
>
> The Word and Markdown converters and the panels live in extra files next to the main script: `viveeditor.docx.iife.js`, `viveeditor.markdown.iife.js` and `viveeditor.panels.iife.js`. They load on first use from the same folder and are checked against `sha384` fingerprints built into that exact version. Short addresses such as `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/viveeditor`, or renamed and combined scripts, cannot find them.

If your site has a Content Security Policy, read [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/) before you go live.

## With npm

### Everything in one package

The `viveeditor` package holds the same editor as the CDN script:

```sh
npm install viveeditor
```

```ts
import { upgradeAll } from 'viveeditor'
import 'viveeditor/style.css'

upgradeAll()
```

With a bundler there are no CDN add-ons. To get Word and Markdown in the File menu, pass the converters as loaders; see [Open, save and print](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/).

### A framework component

React, Vue, Svelte and Angular each have a component package that you install next to `viveeditor`:

```sh
npm install @viveeditor/react viveeditor
```

Use `@viveeditor/vue`, `@viveeditor/svelte` or `@viveeditor/angular` in the same way. For any page there is also `@viveeditor/element`, a `<vive-editor>` form field. Details are on [Frameworks](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/frameworks/).

### Only the parts you need

Every feature is a separate package. `@viveeditor/core` is the engine and has no toolbar; add `@viveeditor/ui` for one:

```sh
npm install @viveeditor/core @viveeditor/ext-basic @viveeditor/ext-list @viveeditor/ui
```

The full list is on [Packages](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/packages/).

## Stylesheets

- CDN: `viveeditor.css` from the same version folder as the script.
- `viveeditor` and the framework components: `import 'viveeditor/style.css'` once.
- Angular: add `node_modules/viveeditor/dist/viveeditor.css` to `styles` in `angular.json`.
- Your own selection of packages: `@viveeditor/core/style.css`, `@viveeditor/ui/style.css` if you use the toolbar, and the `style.css` of each extension that has one: `ext-code-block`, `ext-embed`, `ext-footnote`, `ext-image`, `ext-math`, `ext-mention`, `ext-search`, `ext-table` and `ext-task-list`.

```ts
import '@viveeditor/core/style.css'
import '@viveeditor/ui/style.css'
import '@viveeditor/ext-table/style.css'
```

Formulas also need KaTeX's own stylesheet, `katex/dist/katex.min.css`.

## Requirements

- Node.js 20.19 or newer for your build tools. The npm packages declare it in `engines`.
- React 18 or 19, Vue 3.5, Svelte 5, or Angular 21 or 22 for the component packages.
- KaTeX 0.18.2 or newer if you use formulas. Older versions are refused.
- PHP 8.4 or newer for `viveeditor/sanitizer`, and Laravel 12 or newer for `viveeditor/laravel`.

## Pin the version

All npm packages are released together with the same version number, so install every viveEditor package at the same version. For the CDN script, always write the exact version (`viveeditor@x.y.z`); its add-ons are checked against fingerprints built into that version. Before 1.0 a minor version can contain breaking changes; see [Versioning](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/versioning/).

## Next steps

- [Your first editor](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/first-editor/): textarea, `mountEditor` or `Editor.create`.
- [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/): clean the posted HTML before you store it.

---

# Your first editor

> Turn a textarea into an editor, mount one into any element, or build it from Editor.create and createUI, then read its HTML.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/first-editor/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

There are three ways to start an editor: upgrade a textarea in a form, mount an editor into any element with `mountEditor`, or build one yourself from `Editor.create` and `createUI`. This page shows each, then how to read the content, listen for changes, and set the label and the language.

## Upgrade a textarea

This is the shortest way, and it works with the CDN script or with npm.

1. Load `viveeditor.css` and `viveeditor.classic.iife.js` with your exact version, as shown on [Installation](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/).
2. Add `data-editor` to the textarea. Keep its `name`, and a `<label for>` that points at it.
3. On the server, read the field as usual and sanitize the HTML before you store it; see [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/).

```html
<form method="post">
  <label for="body">Article</label>
  <textarea id="body" name="body" data-editor required></textarea>
  <button>Publish</button>
</form>
```

The textarea stays in the form, hidden, and always holds the latest HTML (`''` when the document is empty). It fires `input` on every change. With `required`, an empty editor cancels the submit, marks itself `aria-invalid="true"`, fires a `vive:invalid` event on the textarea and takes the focus. While images are still uploading, the submit waits and goes out once they are done. Add `data-files="false"` to a textarea to hide its File menu.

### From your own code

With npm, call `upgradeAll()` to upgrade every `textarea[data-editor]`, or `upgradeTextarea()` for one:

```ts
import { upgradeTextarea } from 'viveeditor'
import 'viveeditor/style.css'

const field = await upgradeTextarea(document.querySelector('#body'), {
  label: 'Article body',
  ui: { locale: 'en' },
})

console.log(field.editor.getHTML())
```

`upgradeAll(root, options)` limits the search to `root`. Calling `upgradeTextarea` twice at the same time returns the same promise. `field.destroy()` brings the textarea back and leaves the final HTML in it. Pass `ui: false` to leave out the toolbar.

## Mount into any element

`mountEditor` puts the full editor, with every extension and the toolbar, into any element. The framework components are built on it.

```ts
import { mountEditor } from 'viveeditor'
import 'viveeditor/style.css'

const mount = mountEditor(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  value: '<p>Hello</p>',
  locale: 'en',
  label: 'Article body',
  onChange: (html) => console.log(html),
})

const editor = await mount.ready
```

- The value is HTML, and an empty document is `''`.
- `getValue()`, `setValue(html)`, `setEditable(editable)` and `destroy()` control it. `setValue` with a new value does not call `onChange` and does not go into the undo history.
- `extensions` replaces the default set; `ui: false` drops the toolbar.
- If you call `destroy()` before the editor is ready, `ready` rejects with `MountDestroyedError`.
- No File menu converters are loaded by default; pass them in `ui.files`.

## Build it yourself

`Editor.create` gives you the engine with only the extensions you list. `createUI` adds the toolbar, the selection bubble, the `/` menu and the panels.

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import '@viveeditor/core/style.css'
import { basicExtensions } from '@viveeditor/ext-basic'
import { listExtensions } from '@viveeditor/ext-list'
import { createUI } from '@viveeditor/ui'
import '@viveeditor/ui/style.css'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [...basicExtensions, ...listExtensions],
  content: '<p>Hello <strong>world</strong></p>',
  label: 'Article body',
})

const ui = createUI(editor, { locale: 'en', theme: 'auto' })
```

`createUI` mounts next to the editing area and is removed when the editor is destroyed. It shows only the tools whose commands are registered, so a tool appears once you add its extension. `ui.destroy()` removes it earlier. The options are covered on [Toolbar and shortcuts](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/toolbar-and-shortcuts/).

## Read the content

- `editor.getHTML()` returns the document as HTML.
- `editor.getJSON()` returns ProseMirror JSON, the canonical storage format.
- `editor.getText()` returns plain text, one line per block.
- `editor.isEmpty` tells you whether the document is empty.
- `editor.setContent(content)` loads HTML or JSON. It does not go into the undo history.

Store either HTML or JSON. Both stay readable by later 0.x versions; see [Versioning](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/versioning/).

## Listen for changes

```ts
const stop = editor.on('change', ({ editor }) => {
  console.log(editor.getHTML())
})

editor.on('error', ({ error }) => console.error(error))
```

- `change` fires when the document changes.
- `update` fires on any state change, such as a new selection.
- `focus`, `blur`, `destroy` and `error` are also available.
- `on` returns a function that removes the listener; `off` does the same.

An error thrown inside one listener does not stop the others. It is reported through the `error` event.

## Label and language

Give every editor a `label`, such as `label: 'Article body'`. Screen readers announce it as the name of the editing area. With a textarea, keep a visible `<label for>`; the editor takes its name from it when you pass no `label`.

The interface speaks Turkish and English. Pass `locale` to choose. Without it, the editor follows `<html lang="...">`, then the browser language: anything starting with `tr` gives Turkish, everything else English. To change single strings, pass `messages` to `createUI`, for example `createUI(editor, { messages: { toolbar: 'Formatting' } })`.

## Next steps

- [Frameworks](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/frameworks/): the same editor in React, Vue, Svelte and Angular.
- [Images and uploads](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/images-and-uploads/): connect your upload endpoint.

# Frameworks

> Use viveEditor in React, Vue, Svelte and Angular, or as a <vive-editor> form field, with notes for server rendering.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/frameworks/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

viveEditor has a small component package for React, Vue, Svelte and Angular, and a `<vive-editor>` custom element for any page. Each one gives you the same editor as the one-script build, with every extension and the toolbar, and keeps no editor logic of its own.

## What every component shares

- The value is HTML, and an empty document is `''`.
- Pass `extensions` to choose your own list, or `ui: false` to leave out the toolbar. `ui` also takes the toolbar options, such as `{ theme: 'dark' }`.
- `locale` picks Turkish or English, and `label` names the editing area for screen readers.
- A new value from outside is applied without firing a change event and without entering the undo history. Setting the current value again does nothing.
- File menu converters are not loaded by default. Pass them in `ui.files`; see [Open, save and print](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/).
- Load the styles once with `import 'viveeditor/style.css'`.

Install the component next to `viveeditor`:

```sh
npm install @viveeditor/react viveeditor
```

## React

React 18 and 19.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { ViveEditor } from '@viveeditor/react'
import 'viveeditor/style.css'

export function ArticleForm() {
  const [html, setHtml] = useState('')
  return <ViveEditor value={html} onChange={setHtml} locale="en" label="Article body" />
}
```

- Use `value` with `onChange`, or `defaultValue` alone.
- `onReady`, `onFocus`, `onBlur` and `onError` receive the editor or the error. `editable`, `id`, `className` and `style` are also accepted.
- A `ref` on the component gives you the `Editor`.
- `useViveEditor(options)` returns `{ ref, editor }` for your own markup: put `ref` on a `div`.
- If the component unmounts before the editor is ready, as in StrictMode, the editor is destroyed as soon as it exists and `onReady` is never called.

## Vue

Vue 3.5.

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { ViveEditor } from '@viveeditor/vue'
import 'viveeditor/style.css'

const html = ref('')
</script>

<template>
  <ViveEditor v-model="html" locale="en" label="Article body" />
</template>
```

- Props: `v-model`, `extensions`, `ui`, `locale`, `label`, `editable`.
- Events: `ready`, `focus`, `blur` and `error`. The component exposes `editor`.
- `useViveEditor(() => options)` returns `{ el, editor }` for your own markup.

## Svelte

Svelte 5.

```svelte
<script>
  import { ViveEditor } from '@viveeditor/svelte'
  import 'viveeditor/style.css'
  let html = $state('')
</script>

<ViveEditor bind:value={html} locale="en" label="Article body" />
```

- `bind:value` and `bind:editor` keep the HTML and the editor in your state.
- Callbacks: `onchange`, `onready`, `onfocus`, `onblur` and `onerror`.
- The `use:viveEditor` action puts the editor on any element and takes the same options.

## Angular

Angular 21 and 22, with `ngModel` or reactive forms.

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core'
import { FormControl, ReactiveFormsModule } from '@angular/forms'
import { ViveEditorComponent } from '@viveeditor/angular'

@Component({
  selector: 'app-article-form',
  imports: [ViveEditorComponent, ReactiveFormsModule],
  template: `<vive-ng-editor [formControl]="body" locale="en" label="Article body" />`,
})
export class ArticleForm {
  body = new FormControl('')
}
```

- The selector is `vive-ng-editor`. `vive-editor` is the custom element below.
- Inputs: `extensions`, `ui`, `locale`, `label`, `readonly`.
- Outputs: `ready`, `editorFocus` and `editorBlur`. The component's `editor` property gives the editor.
- Add `node_modules/viveeditor/dist/viveeditor.css` to `styles` in `angular.json`.

## The `<vive-editor>` element

`@viveeditor/element` works as a form field on any page and in any framework.

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@viveeditor/element/define'
</script>

<form>
  <vive-editor name="body" required locale="en" label="Article body"></vive-editor>
</form>
```

- It sends its HTML with the form, returns to its first value when the form resets, and blocks submit while `required` and empty.
- Attributes: `value` (the first value), `name`, `locale`, `label`, `readonly`, `disabled`, `required` and `toolbar="false"`.
- It fires `input` on every change and `change` on blur when the value changed.
- It uses no shadow DOM, so your page styles reach it. Moving it in the page keeps its value.
- `defineViveEditor('my-editor')` registers it under another tag name.

The element is an npm package; the CDN script does not include it.

## Server rendering

With Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit or Angular SSR, the server renders an empty element and the editor starts in the browser. Each package mounts only there: React in `useEffect`, Vue in `onMounted`, Svelte through its action, Angular in `afterNextRender`, and the element in `connectedCallback`. The React package is marked `'use client'`.

When you print stored HTML on a page, pass it through the server sanitizer first; see [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/).

---

# Toolbar and shortcuts

> The floating toolbar, selection bubble, / menu, block menu, word count, readability score and every keyboard shortcut.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/toolbar-and-shortcuts/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

The viveEditor interface comes from `@viveeditor/ui`: a floating toolbar below the text, a small bubble when you select text, a block menu that opens with `/`, and a word count. This page explains what each part does, how to turn it off and which keyboard shortcuts exist. The one-script build and the framework components show the toolbar already; with the npm packages you call `createUI` yourself.

## Set up the interface

```ts
import { createUI } from '@viveeditor/ui'
import '@viveeditor/ui/style.css'

const ui = createUI(editor, { locale: 'en', theme: 'auto' })
```

`createUI` mounts into the element that holds the editor and removes itself when the editor is destroyed. It only shows tools whose commands are registered: without the table extension there is no table button. The interface talks to the editor only through commands and queries.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `locale` | `'tr'` or `'en'`. Without it, the page's `lang` decides: Turkish if it starts with `tr`, English otherwise. |
| `messages` | Replaces some of the labels with your own text. |
| `theme` | `'light'` (default), `'dark'` or `'auto'`. Use the `--ve-accent` CSS variable for your brand colour. |
| `readability` | `'atesman'`, `'flesch'` or `false`. The default follows the language. |
| `bubble` | `false` turns off the selection bubble. |
| `slash` | `false` turns off the `/` menu. |
| `source` | `false` removes the HTML source button. |
| `files` | The File menu; `false` hides it. See [Open, save and print](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/). |
| `plugins` | Extra menus such as mentions, emoji and templates plug in here from `@viveeditor/ui/extras`. |
| `onError` | Receives errors raised in the interface. |

## Floating toolbar

The toolbar sits below the text and stays at the bottom of the screen while you scroll a long article. On phones it moves above the on-screen keyboard.

From left to right: the block type button; bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and inline code; text colour and highlight; bulleted list, numbered list, task list, quote, table, image and video; alignment; link and find and replace; undo, redo, File and HTML source. The word count sits at the end.

Below 560 pixels only bold, italic and link stay in place, and the other tools move to the "More tools" menu. In wider spaces, tools that do not fit move into that menu in a fixed order; the menu shows only the tools that moved.

The HTML source button opens the document's HTML in an editable text area. While it is open the other tools are disabled; when you close it, your changes are applied to the editor.

## Selection bubble

When you select text, a small toolbar opens just above the selection. On touch screens it opens below the selection, so your finger does not cover it. It holds bold, italic, link and inline code; plugins such as the [AI assistant](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/ai-assistant/) add their own buttons. The bubble does not open while an image is selected. `Esc` closes it, and `bubble: false` removes it.

## The / menu

Type `/` at the start of a paragraph to open the block menu. The letters you type next filter the list. Search ignores Turkish letter marks, and English keywords also work (`/table`, `/video`).

The entries are: Heading 1, 2 and 3, bulleted list, numbered list, task list, quote, code block, table (3×3 with a header row), image, video and divider. Image and video do not insert anything directly; they open their panel.

Move with `↑` and `↓`, choose with `Enter` or `Tab`, and close with `Esc`. Focus stays in the text, and screen readers announce the active entry. The mention, emoji, formula, footnote and template plugins add their own entries.

## Block menu

The button at the start of the toolbar shows the type of the block at the cursor, such as Paragraph, Heading 2 or Quote. Open it to switch between paragraph, Heading 1–3, the lists, quote and code block. Choosing Paragraph also removes a list or quote around the block.

## Word count and readability

The count at the end of the toolbar shows how many words the document has. If you set a [character limit](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/character-limit/), it shows the characters used and the limit instead. The count updates when you pause typing.

Click the count to open the "Text statistics" panel:

- the readability score (0–100) and its band,
- the number of words and sentences,
- the average sentence length,
- the reading time (based on 200 words per minute).

The Turkish interface uses the Ateşman formula and the English interface uses Flesch. Pass `readability` to choose another formula; `false` hides the score and keeps the statistics. The score needs at least 10 words.

| Band | Ateşman | Flesch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Very easy | 90 and above | 80 and above |
| Easy | 70–89 | 60–79 |
| Fair | 50–69 | 50–59 |
| Hard | 30–49 | 30–49 |
| Very hard | below 30 | below 30 |

To use the same measure in your own code, call `measureText(text, 'flesch')` from `@viveeditor/ui`.

## Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use `⌘` instead of `Ctrl` and `⌥` instead of `Alt`. The toolbar hints show each shortcut for your operating system. A shortcut works when its extension is loaded.

| Action | Windows and Linux | Mac |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bold | `Ctrl+B` | `⌘+B` |
| Italic | `Ctrl+I` | `⌘+I` |
| Underline | `Ctrl+U` | `⌘+U` |
| Strikethrough | `Ctrl+Shift+S` | `⌘+⇧+S` |
| Inline code | `Ctrl+E` | `⌘+E` |
| Highlight | `Ctrl+Shift+H` | `⌘+⇧+H` |
| Heading 1–6 | `Ctrl+Alt+1` … `6` | `⌘+⌥+1` … `6` |
| Bulleted list | `Ctrl+Shift+8` | `⌘+⇧+8` |
| Numbered list | `Ctrl+Shift+7` | `⌘+⇧+7` |
| Task list | `Ctrl+Shift+9` | `⌘+⇧+9` |
| Quote | `Ctrl+Shift+B` | `⌘+⇧+B` |
| Code block | `Ctrl+Alt+C` | `⌘+⌥+C` |
| Align left | `Ctrl+Shift+L` | `⌘+⇧+L` |
| Align center | `Ctrl+Shift+E` | `⌘+⇧+E` |
| Align right | `Ctrl+Shift+R` | `⌘+⇧+R` |
| Justify | `Ctrl+Shift+J` | `⌘+⇧+J` |
| Link | `Ctrl+K` | `⌘+K` |
| Find and replace | `Ctrl+F` | `⌘+F` |
| Undo | `Ctrl+Z` | `⌘+Z` |
| Redo | `Ctrl+Shift+Z` or `Ctrl+Y` | `⌘+⇧+Z` or `⌘+Y` |
| New line in the same paragraph | `Shift+Enter` | `⇧+Enter` |
| Move to the toolbar | `Alt+F10` | `⌥+F10` |
| AI assistant | `Ctrl+J` | `⌘+J` |

The AI shortcut works only when the [AI assistant](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/ai-assistant/) plugin is added.

### Moving around

- In the toolbar, `←` and `→` move between buttons, and `Home` and `End` jump to the first and last. `Esc` takes you back to the text.
- In a list, `Tab` indents the item and `Shift+Tab` outdents it.
- In a table, `Tab` moves to the next cell and adds a row in the last cell; `Shift+Tab` goes back.
- In a code block, `Tab` indents and `Shift+Tab` outdents.
- To leave a table or code block with the keyboard, press `Esc` and then `Tab`; focus moves to the next element after the editor.
- Panels and menus close with `Esc`, and focus returns to their button or to the text.

### Typing shortcuts

Some marks typed at the start of a line turn into blocks:

| Type | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `#` to `######` and a space | Heading 1–6 |
| `-`, `*` or `+` and a space | Bulleted list |
| `1.` and a space | Numbered list (another number starts from that number) |
| `[ ]` and a space | Task list (`[x]` starts checked) |
| `>` and a space | Quote |
| `` ``` `` and a space | Code block (you can add a language name) |
| `---` | Divider |

Inside text, `**bold**` or `__bold__`, `*italic*` or `_italic_`, `~~strikethrough~~` and backticks for inline code are formatted as you type.

## Can I turn the toolbar off completely?

Yes. Pass ui false to the framework components or mountEditor; with the npm packages, do not call createUI. Keyboard shortcuts come from the extensions, so they still work without the toolbar.

## Why does the readability score show a dash?

The score needs at least 10 words. For shorter text the panel says "Write at least 10 words for a score." Words, sentences and reading time are still shown.

## Why is a tool missing?

The toolbar only shows tools whose commands are registered. Without the table extension there is no table button, for example. In narrow spaces some tools move to the More tools menu.

---

# Images and uploads

> Set up the image extension, write the upload function, handle progress and abort, secure your server and track alt text.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/images-and-uploads/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

`@viveeditor/ext-image` handles inserting images, uploading files and image sizes. Every image address and every file is checked before it reaches the document; an upload function that you write sends files to your server. This page covers setup, the upload function contract, what your server must do and the alt text reminders.

## Setup

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import { Image } from '@viveeditor/ext-image'
import '@viveeditor/ext-image/style.css'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [
    Image.configure({
      upload,
      onError: ({ code, fileName }) => console.warn(code, fileName),
    }),
  ],
})
```

In the one-script build the image extension comes without an uploader: images can only be added by address. To upload files, set up the extension from npm with your own `upload` function.

## Options

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `upload` | `null` | The function that sends files to your server. |
| `rehost` | `null` | The function that moves an image from another site to your server. |
| `remoteImages` | `'allow'` | Images pasted from other sites: `'allow'`, `'drop'` or `'rehost'`. |
| `allowBase64` | `false` | Allows images embedded as data addresses. |
| `maxBase64Length` | `1500000` | The maximum number of characters in one data address. |
| `insecure` | `'upgrade'` | Turns `http:` addresses into `https:`; `'block'` rejects them. |
| `allowRelative` | `false` | Allows relative image addresses. |
| `mimeTypes` | png, jpeg, gif, webp, avif | Accepted file types. |
| `maxSize` | 10 MB | The largest size of one file. |
| `maxFiles` | `10` | How many files can be added at once. |
| `concurrency` | `3` | How many files upload at the same time. |
| `timeout` | 60 s | The longest time one upload may take. |
| `maxPreviewPixels` | 25 million | Files above this pixel count get no preview. |
| `requireAlt` | `'warn'` | Shows a badge on images without alt text; `'off'` turns it off. |
| `labels` | English | Labels for uploading, failure and missing alt text. |
| `onError` | `null` | Receives `{ code, fileName }` for a failed file. |

## The upload function

The upload function receives a file and a context, and returns the image address:

```ts
import type { ImageUploader } from '@viveeditor/ext-image'

const upload: ImageUploader = async (file, { signal, onProgress }) => {
  const body = new FormData()
  body.append('file', file)
  const response = await fetch('/uploads', { method: 'POST', body, signal })
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Upload failed')
  const { url, width, height } = await response.json()
  return { src: url, width, height }
}
```

- Return an address string or a `{ src, width, height }` object. `width` and `height` are optional, but it is best when your server measures and returns the real size.
- The returned address goes through the same check: `blob:` never passes, and `data:` passes only with `allowBase64`. If it fails, the image is not inserted.
- If the function throws, a box saying "Image could not be added" stays in place of the image and `onError` is called.
- Before a file reaches your function, its type, size and first bytes are checked. This check gives the writer early feedback; your server is the security boundary.

During an upload, a placeholder with a progress bar stands where the image will go. The placeholder is never written to the document, and `getHTML()` never contains it.

### Progress

`onProgress` expects a value between 0 and 1; values outside that range are clamped. `fetch` does not report upload progress. If you want a progress bar, you can use `XMLHttpRequest`:

```ts
import type { ImageUploader } from '@viveeditor/ext-image'

const upload: ImageUploader = (file, { signal, onProgress }) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const request = new XMLHttpRequest()
    request.open('POST', '/uploads')
    request.responseType = 'json'
    request.upload.onprogress = (event) => {
      if (event.lengthComputable) onProgress(event.loaded / event.total)
    }
    request.onload = () => {
      if (request.status !== 200) return reject(new Error('Upload failed'))
      const { url, width, height } = request.response
      resolve({ src: url, width, height })
    }
    request.onerror = () => reject(new Error('Upload failed'))
    request.onabort = () => reject(signal.reason)
    signal.addEventListener('abort', () => request.abort())
    const body = new FormData()
    body.append('file', file)
    request.send(body)
  })
```

### Abort

Every upload has its own `AbortSignal`. The signal is aborted when:

- the writer deletes the placeholder or undoes the insert,
- the content is replaced with `setContent`,
- the editor is destroyed,
- the `timeout` runs out.

Pass the signal to `fetch` or `XMLHttpRequest` so the request to your server stops too. The result of an aborted upload is never inserted.

### Error codes

`onError` receives only a code and the file name; server responses and file contents are never passed on.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `TYPE` | The file type is not allowed, or its content does not match its type. |
| `SIZE` | The file is larger than `maxSize`. |
| `COUNT` | More than `maxFiles` files were added at once. |
| `TIMEOUT` | The upload did not finish within `timeout`. |
| `UPLOAD` | The upload function threw an error. |
| `SOURCE` | The address the function returned failed the check. |

### Pending uploads

`editor.query.isUploading()` returns `true` while an upload is running. `editor.query.pendingUploads()` counts running and failed uploads as `{ uploading, failed }`. If you submit the form yourself, wait with these queries; the one-script build does it for you.

## Server checklist

The editor checks every address and file, but the browser is not a security boundary. Your server must also:

- Sanitize the posted HTML again and allow only the `https` image addresses you expect. See [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/).
- Re-validate and re-encode every upload. This strips EXIF and GPS data and polyglot files. Return the real width and height.
- Serve uploads from a cookieless domain, with a server-set `Content-Type` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- Require authentication, a CSRF token and a rate limit on the upload endpoint.
- Restrict `img-src` in your Content Security Policy. See [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/).
- Guard against SSRF if your server fetches remote images (for `remoteImages: 'rehost'`).

## Images pasted from other sites

Content copied from another page brings the addresses of that site's images. When a reader's browser shows them, it tells that site who read the page and when. `remoteImages` decides what happens to these images:

| Value | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `'allow'` | Default. The image keeps its original address. |
| `'drop'` | Pasted `https` images are removed. |
| `'rehost'` | Your `rehost` function moves the image to your server. Without that function, the image is removed. |

The `rehost` function receives an address instead of a file, gets the same context (`signal`, `onProgress`) and returns an address like the upload function. For a hardened setup, choose `'drop'` or `'rehost'`.

## Alt text

The image panel has an alt text field and a "Decorative, no description needed" checkbox. Images that never got alt text show a "No alt text" badge inside the editor; the badge never enters the saved HTML. `requireAlt: 'off'` turns the badge off.

The saved value keeps two cases apart: alt text left empty counts as missing, while an image marked decorative is saved with an empty `alt=""`. Before publishing, `editor.query.imagesWithoutAlt()` counts the missing ones so you can remind the writer.

## Width and height

Every saved image carries `width` and `height`, so the layout does not jump while the page loads. The values come from:

- the size your upload function returns, which always wins,
- otherwise, for PNG, GIF and WebP files, the size read from the file.

In the editor, drag the handle at the image corner to change its width; the height follows the ratio. The 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% buttons in the image panel scale the image to the content width.

Saved images are written with `loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"` and `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`. Add this rule to the pages that show the content:

```css
img {
  max-width: 100%;
  height: auto;
}
```

## Image panel

The image button in the toolbar or the "Image" entry in the `/` menu opens the panel. With an upload function, a "Choose from device" button appears, and you can also drag and drop or paste an image into the editor. Enter an image address that starts with `https`; the panel warns about an address it cannot use. With an image selected, the panel lets you change its alt text and size.

## What happens if I do not pass an upload function?

Images can only be added by https address. The "Choose from device" button in the image panel is hidden, and dropped or pasted files are not uploaded.

## Can images be embedded in the document as base64?

Not by default. With allowBase64 true, data addresses of type png, jpeg, gif, webp and avif are accepted, limited by maxBase64Length. SVG is never accepted.

## What happens if the form is submitted during an upload?

With the one-script build, the form waits until uploads finish and then submits itself. If an upload fails while it waits, the submit is cancelled and an error message appears.

---

# Video and audio embeds

> Turn YouTube, Vimeo and Spotify links into safe players, with the preview card, activateEmbeds, server checks and CSP settings.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/video-embeds/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

`@viveeditor/ext-embed` turns YouTube, Vimeo and Spotify links into players. The saved HTML never keeps the address it was given; it stores only the provider and the video id, and every player address is rebuilt from them. This page covers setup, loading players on the published page, and the server and Content Security Policy settings.

## Setup

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import { Embed } from '@viveeditor/ext-embed'
import '@viveeditor/ext-embed/style.css'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [Embed.configure({ providers: ['youtube', 'vimeo'], facade: true })],
})
```

The one-script build already includes the extension with all three providers.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `providers` | `['youtube', 'vimeo', 'spotify']` | The enabled providers. |
| `facade` | `false` | With `true`, the saved HTML holds a link instead of a player. |
| `pasteToEmbed` | `true` | Turns a link pasted on an empty line into a player. |
| `maxEmbeds` | `50` | The maximum number of players in one document. |
| `labels` | English | Labels for the play button and for unsupported content. |

## Add a video

- Paste just the link on an empty line. It turns into a player; one undo turns it back into a link.
- Press the video button in the toolbar or the "Video" entry in the `/` menu. Enter the link and a title in the panel; screen readers announce that title.
- In code, use `editor.commands.insertEmbed(url)` to insert and `editor.commands.setEmbedTitle(title)` to change the title.

Inside the editor a card stands in for the player, with the provider name, the title and a play button. Nothing loads from the provider until play is pressed.

## Supported links

| Provider | Accepted links | Player address |
| --- | --- | --- |
| YouTube | `youtube.com/watch?v=…`, `youtu.be/…`, `/shorts/`, `/live/` and `/embed/` addresses; start time from `t` or `start` | `www.youtube-nocookie.com` |
| Vimeo | `vimeo.com/…`, addresses with the private key of unlisted videos, `player.vimeo.com/video/…`; start time from `#t=` | `player.vimeo.com`, with `dnt=1` |
| Spotify | Track, album, playlist, episode, show and artist addresses on `open.spotify.com` | `open.spotify.com/embed` |

Links are parsed as addresses and the host name is compared exactly. Short links and redirects are never followed, and nothing is requested from the provider.

## Saved HTML

The player is always rebuilt from the provider and id; `sandbox`, `allow` and `referrerpolicy` are fixed and never read from the content. The saved HTML holds a `div[data-embed]` wrapper in one of two forms:

- `facade: false` (default): the wrapper holds the player `iframe`. The player loads from the provider when the reader opens the page.
- `facade: true`: the wrapper holds a link to the video's page at the provider. The player loads when the reader clicks.

When you save as Word or Markdown, players are written as links.

### Publish facade output

On the page that shows content saved with `facade: true`, call `activateEmbeds()`. Clicking the link replaces it with the player and starts playback:

```ts
import { activateEmbeds } from '@viveeditor/ext-embed/activate'

activateEmbeds(document.querySelector('article'), { providers: ['youtube', 'vimeo'] })
```

The first argument is the root element to search (the whole document if left out), and `providers` lists the allowed providers. The player address is built from the provider and id on the wrapper, never from the link's `href`. Without `activateEmbeds`, the link opens the video on the provider's site.

## On the server

- Clean the HTML on the server too, but never allow every `iframe`. Pass `embeds: true` to `@viveeditor/sanitize`; players are rebuilt from the provider and id. See [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/).
- With your own sanitizer, rebuild players from `div[data-embed]`, or accept only addresses for which `isAllowedEmbedSrc()` returns `true`.

```ts
import { isAllowedEmbedSrc } from '@viveeditor/ext-embed'

const allowed = isAllowedEmbedSrc(src, ['youtube', 'vimeo'])
```

`isAllowedEmbedSrc` checks that the address is exactly the player address the editor builds. In the same package, `matchEmbedUrl(url)` reads the provider and id from a link, and `buildEmbedSrc(attrs)` builds the player address. None of the three needs a browser DOM.

## Content Security Policy and privacy

- List only the providers you enabled in your CSP `frame-src`. With all three: `frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://player.vimeo.com https://open.spotify.com`.
- A player loads content and cookies from the provider. Tell readers about it where your consent rules require it; facade output loads the player only after a click.

> **Referrer-Policy**
>
> A page-wide `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` stops YouTube players from working. This is why players are built with `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.

For the other CSP settings, see [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/).

## Why does the video not load right away in the editor?

Inside the editor a card stands in for the player. Nothing loads from the provider until someone presses play, which protects the writer's privacy and keeps the page light.

## Can I embed videos from other sites?

No. Only YouTube, Vimeo and Spotify are supported. Other links are not turned into players, and the panel lists the supported providers.

## My page sends Referrer-Policy no-referrer. Why does YouTube not work?

YouTube rejects embedded players that arrive without a Referer. A page-wide no-referrer policy stops YouTube players from working.

---

# Tables

> Tables with merged cells, header rows, column widths you can drag, and the table tools in the toolbar.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/tables/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

`@viveeditor/ext-table` adds tables to the editor: merged cells, header rows, column widths set by dragging, and `Tab` to move between cells. The saved HTML carries the column widths, so a table looks the same on any site. This page covers setup, the table tools and keyboard use.

## Setup

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import { Table } from '@viveeditor/ext-table'
import '@viveeditor/ext-table/style.css'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [Table],
})

editor.commands.insertTable({ rows: 3, cols: 3, headerRow: true })
```

The one-script build already includes the table extension.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resizable` | `true` | Lets writers drag a column edge to set its width. |
| `cellMinWidth` | `48` | The smallest column width, in pixels. |
| `maxSize` | `20` | The most rows and columns `insertTable` can add. |

## Insert a table

- The table button in the toolbar opens a 6×6 grid. Choose the size with the mouse or the arrow keys, then click or press `Enter`. The table gets a header row.
- The "Table" entry in the `/` menu inserts a 3×3 table with a header row (`/table`).
- In code, use `insertTable({ rows, cols, headerRow })`. Without values the table is 3×3 and starts with a header row.

A table inserted in an empty paragraph replaces that paragraph. You cannot insert a table inside another table.

## Table tools

While the cursor is inside a table, the table button in the toolbar opens the table tools instead of the grid:

| Group | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Insert | Insert row above, Insert row below, Insert column left, Insert column right |
| Arrange | Merge cells, Split cell, Header row, Widen column, Narrow column |
| Delete | Delete row, Delete column, Delete table |

Tools that cannot run at that moment are shown as disabled. For example, "Merge cells" is not available while a single cell is selected. `Esc` closes the panel.

## Merged cells

Drag with the mouse to select several cells, then choose "Merge cells". To undo a merge, click inside the merged cell and choose "Split cell". Merged cells are kept when you save as Word.

## Header row and column

"Header row" turns the first row into header cells, or back. Header cells are written as `th` in the HTML, so screen readers can announce the column headings. The interface has no button for a header column; use the `editor.commands.toggleHeaderColumn()` command.

## Column widths

With `resizable` on, drag the right edge of a column to change its width. From the keyboard, "Widen column" and "Narrow column" in the table tools change the column at the cursor by 40 pixels. A column cannot be narrower than `cellMinWidth`.

A table with set widths carries a `colgroup` and a `width` style per column in the saved HTML. The table itself gets the total width; if some columns have no width, that total is used as a minimum width. Tables without any set width carry no style.

## Keyboard

- `Tab` moves to the next cell. In the last cell it adds a new row.
- `Shift+Tab` moves to the previous cell.
- `Esc` and then `Tab` moves focus out of the table and the editor.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `insertTable(options)` | Inserts a table. |
| `addRowBefore()`, `addRowAfter()` | Adds a row. |
| `addColumnBefore()`, `addColumnAfter()` | Adds a column. |
| `deleteRow()`, `deleteColumn()`, `deleteTable()` | Deletes the row, column or table. |
| `mergeCells()`, `splitCell()` | Merges or splits cells. |
| `toggleHeaderRow()`, `toggleHeaderColumn()` | Turns the header row or column on or off. |
| `resizeColumn(delta)` | Widens or narrows the column at the cursor, in pixels. |

`editor.query.inTable()` returns `true` while the cursor is inside a table. To test a command first, use the `can` form, such as `editor.can.mergeCells()`.

Tables are also saved to Markdown and Word files; see [Open, save and print](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/).

## Do column widths survive on the published page?

Yes. Widths are written into the saved HTML as a colgroup and styles, so the table looks the same on any site. The server sanitizer keeps table widths.

## Can I put a table inside a table?

No. While the cursor is inside a table, the insert command does nothing; the toolbar's table button opens the table tools instead.

## How do I leave a table with the keyboard?

Press Esc and then Tab. Tab alone moves between cells, so this order moves focus to the next element after the editor.

---

# Code blocks

> Code blocks with a language picker, the default language list and optional Shiki syntax colouring, including a setup without WebAssembly.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/code-blocks/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

`@viveeditor/ext-code-block` adds code blocks with a language picker. Syntax colouring is optional: `CodeHighlight` loads the highlighter you give it only when the page has code, and colours never enter the saved HTML. This page covers the code block, the language list and colouring with Shiki.

## Setup

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import { CodeBlock } from '@viveeditor/ext-code-block'
import { CodeHighlight, shikiHighlighter } from '@viveeditor/ext-code-block/highlight'
import '@viveeditor/ext-code-block/style.css'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [
    CodeBlock,
    CodeHighlight.configure({ highlighter: shikiHighlighter(() => import('shiki')) }),
  ],
})
```

The one-script build already includes the code block, without a highlighter.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `languages` | `DEFAULT_LANGUAGES` | The languages in the picker. |
| `languageLabel` | `'Language'` | The accessible name of the picker. |
| `plainTextLabel` | `'Plain text'` | The option name for a block without a language. |
| `tabSize` | `2` | How many spaces `Tab` inserts. |

## Add a code block

- Type three backticks and a space at the start of a line. To set the language at once, type its name right after the backticks, such as `ts`, then a space.
- `Ctrl+Alt+C` (`⌘+⌥+C` on a Mac) turns the block on and off.
- Choose "Code block" from the block menu or the `/` menu.

If several paragraphs are selected when you turn on a code block, their lines join into one block. Turning the code block off makes each line a separate paragraph.

## Language picker

Each block has a language picker in its top corner. The first option is "Plain text", followed by the `languages` list. A valid language name that is not in the list (from pasted content, for example) is kept and appears in the picker under its own name.

A language name is made of letters, digits and `+ # . -`, is at most 32 characters long and is lowercased. The saved HTML carries the language in two places:

```html
<pre data-language="typescript"><code class="language-typescript">const a = 1</code></pre>
```

When content is loaded, the language is read from the `data-language` attribute or from a class that starts with `language-` or `lang-`.

### Default languages

`DEFAULT_LANGUAGES` holds 19 languages: JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, JSON, Python, PHP, Java, Kotlin, Swift, C#, C++, Go, Rust, Ruby, SQL, Bash, YAML and Markdown. Their values are `javascript`, `typescript`, `html`, `css`, `json`, `python`, `php`, `java`, `kotlin`, `swift`, `csharp`, `cpp`, `go`, `rust`, `ruby`, `sql`, `bash`, `yaml` and `markdown`.

To add a language to the list:

```ts
import { CodeBlock, DEFAULT_LANGUAGES } from '@viveeditor/ext-code-block'

const codeBlock = CodeBlock.configure({
  languages: [...DEFAULT_LANGUAGES, { value: 'dart', label: 'Dart' }],
})
```

## Keyboard in a code block

- `Tab` inserts `tabSize` spaces at the cursor. With several lines selected, it indents each line.
- `Shift+Tab` removes spaces at the start of the line.
- `Enter` starts a new line inside the block. Press `Enter` three times in a row at the end of the block to remove the trailing empty lines and continue in a new paragraph.
- `Backspace` in an empty block turns it into a paragraph.
- `Esc` and then `Tab` moves focus out of the editor.

Commands: `toggleCodeBlock(language)`, `setCodeBlockLanguage(language)`. `editor.query.codeBlockLanguage()` returns the language of the block at the cursor.

## Syntax colouring

`CodeHighlight` colours only blocks that have a language. It loads the highlighter the first time such a block is on the page, caches the results and applies the colours only to the editor view, never to the saved HTML.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `highlighter` | `null` | The highlighter function. Without it, nothing is coloured. |
| `delay` | `120` | How many milliseconds after a typing pause colouring runs. |
| `cacheSize` | `200` | How many blocks the cache keeps. |

`shikiHighlighter(load, options)` is a ready bridge for [Shiki](https://shiki.style). The default themes are `github-light-default` and `github-dark-default`; pass `{ themes: { light, dark } }` for others. Colours follow the light and dark theme of the interface. If Shiki does not know a language or fails, that block stays uncoloured.

You can also write your own highlighter: a function that takes `(code, language)` and returns `{ from, to, style }` pieces is enough.

### When your CSP does not allow WebAssembly

Shiki's default regular expression engine uses WebAssembly. If your page's Content Security Policy does not allow WebAssembly, set up Shiki with its JavaScript regular expression engine and pass it to `shikiHighlighter`. `shikiHighlighter` only needs a `codeToTokens` method on the loaded object:

```ts
import { CodeHighlight, shikiHighlighter } from '@viveeditor/ext-code-block/highlight'

const loadShiki = async () => {
  const { createHighlighterCore } = await import('shiki/core')
  const { createJavaScriptRegexEngine } = await import('shiki/engine/javascript')
  return createHighlighterCore({
    themes: [
      import('shiki/themes/github-light-default.mjs'),
      import('shiki/themes/github-dark-default.mjs'),
    ],
    langs: [import('shiki/langs/javascript.mjs'), import('shiki/langs/typescript.mjs')],
    engine: createJavaScriptRegexEngine(),
  })
}

const highlight = CodeHighlight.configure({ highlighter: shikiHighlighter(loadShiki) })
```

With this setup only the languages you load in `langs` are coloured; the others stay plain. The themes must be the `shikiHighlighter` defaults or match its `themes` option.

## Code blocks in files

Saving to Markdown writes code blocks as fenced blocks with their language, and opening Markdown reads them back. A Word file keeps the code but not its language. See [Open, save and print](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/).

To show colours on the published page, run a highlighter there as well; the language is in the `class` attribute.

## Do the colours end up in the saved HTML?

No. Colouring is shown only inside the editor. The saved HTML carries the language, not the colours.

## What happens to a language that is not in the list?

A valid language name in pasted or loaded content is kept and appears in the picker under its own name. You can also replace the list with the languages option.

## Can I use code blocks without colouring?

Yes. CodeHighlight is optional. The code block in the one-script build also comes without a highlighter.

---

# Find and replace

> Find and replace that matches Turkish capitals correctly, with match case, whole word and replace all options.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/find-and-replace/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

`@viveeditor/ext-search` adds find and replace to the editor. It matches Turkish capitals correctly: a search for `istanbul` also finds `İstanbul` and `ISTANBUL`. The panel comes from `@viveeditor/ui` and opens with `Ctrl+F` (`⌘+F` on a Mac). This page covers the panel, the matching rules and the commands.

## Setup

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import { Search } from '@viveeditor/ext-search'
import '@viveeditor/ext-search/style.css'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [Search],
})
```

The one-script build already includes the search extension. Its only option is `maxQueryLength` (default 200): longer search text is cut to that length.

## The find and replace panel

`Ctrl+F` or the "Find and replace" button in the toolbar opens the panel. If text is selected and fits on one line, it fills the search field. Matches are highlighted in the document.

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Find | The text to search for. Results update as you type. |
| Previous match, Next match | Move between matches. |
| Match case | When on, letters must match exactly. |
| Whole word only | When on, matches inside a longer word do not count. |
| Counter | Shows which match you are on, such as `3 of 12`. With no matches it says "No results". |
| Replace with | The new text. Leave it empty to delete the matches. |
| Replace | Replaces the selected match and moves to the next. |
| Replace all | Replaces every match in one step. |

Keyboard:

- In the search field, `Enter` goes to the next match and `Shift+Enter` to the previous one.
- In the "Replace with" field, `Enter` replaces the next match.
- `Esc` closes the panel, removes the highlights and takes you back to the text.

## Turkish capitals

With match case off, every letter is matched with both the general and the Turkish case rules:

| Letter searched | Letters matched |
| --- | --- |
| `i` | i, I, İ |
| `ı` | ı, I |
| `İ` | İ, i |
| `I` | I, i, ı |

For example, `istanbul` finds `İstanbul`, `Istanbul` and `ISTANBUL`, and `ılık` finds `ILIK`. Only case is ignored: `s` and `ş`, `c` and `ç`, `o` and `ö` are different letters.

With "Match case" on, these rules are off and the text is searched exactly as typed.

## Replacing

"Replace" first selects a match; when a match is selected, pressing it again replaces that match and selects the next one. "Replace all" replaces every match in the document in a single step, so one undo brings them all back.

## Commands

You can do the same in code, without the panel:

```ts
editor.commands.setSearch({ query: 'istanbul', replace: 'İstanbul', wholeWord: true })
const { total } = editor.query.searchStatus()
if (total > 0) editor.commands.replaceAll()
editor.commands.clearSearch()
```

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `setSearch(terms)` | Starts or updates the search: `query`, `replace`, `caseSensitive`, `wholeWord`. |
| `findNext()`, `findPrevious()` | Selects the next or previous match. |
| `replaceNext()` | Replaces the selected match. |
| `replaceAll()` | Replaces every match. |
| `clearSearch()` | Removes the search and the highlights. |

`editor.query.searchStatus()` returns `{ total, current }`: the number of matches and the position of the selected match (`0` when none is selected). To reuse the same Turkish-aware matching elsewhere, the package exports `caseInsensitivePattern(text)`, which returns a regular expression pattern.

## Why does a search for "istanbul" find "İstanbul"?

With match case off, search uses both the general and the Turkish case rules. So i matches İ and I, and ı matches I.

## Can I undo Replace all?

Yes. All replacements happen in one step, so one undo brings everything back.

## Does search treat ş and s as the same letter?

No. Only the difference between capital and small letters is ignored; different letters such as ş and s or ç and c stay apart.

---

# Character limit

> Count characters and set a limit; typing stops at the limit, pasted text is trimmed and the toolbar shows how much is left.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/character-limit/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

`@viveeditor/ext-character-count` counts the characters in the document and can set a limit. At the limit typing stops, pasted text is trimmed to fit the space left, and deleting always works. The count in the toolbar shows the characters used and allowed. This page covers setup, what counts and how the interface shows the limit.

## Setup

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import { CharacterCount } from '@viveeditor/ext-character-count'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [CharacterCount.configure({ limit: 280 })],
})
```

The extension's only option is `limit`. The default `null` sets no limit and only counts. The limit must be a positive whole number; any other value means no limit.

The character count is not in the one-script build. To keep the ready-made extension list, add it to the list in the framework components or with `mountEditor`:

```ts
import { CharacterCount } from '@viveeditor/ext-character-count'
import { classicPreset, mountEditor } from 'viveeditor'

const mount = mountEditor(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [...classicPreset('en'), CharacterCount.configure({ limit: 280 })],
  locale: 'en',
})
```

## How the limit works

- Typing stops at the limit.
- Pasted or dropped text is trimmed to fit the space left.
- Deleting always works. Any change that does not add characters is accepted.
- Content you load yourself with `content` or `setContent` is not cut. If it is over the limit, the writer can make changes that add characters only after getting below the limit.

The limit in the browser helps the writer, but it is not a security measure. Check the length on your server too.

## What counts

- Every character in the text, spaces included.
- Turkish letters and most emoji count as one character each. Counting is by Unicode code point, so an emoji built from several parts (such as skin tone or family emoji) counts once per part.
- Images, videos, line breaks and paragraph breaks do not count.

## The count in the toolbar

With a limit, the count at the end of the toolbar shows the characters used and allowed, such as `120/280 characters`, instead of the word count. Numbers are formatted for the interface language.

- At 90 percent of the limit, the count turns to the warning colour.
- At the limit, it turns to the danger colour and screen readers announce "Character limit reached".

Clicking the count opens the text statistics panel: readability, words, sentences and reading time. See [Toolbar and shortcuts](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/toolbar-and-shortcuts/).

## Read the count in code

```ts
const used = editor.query.characterCount()
const limit = editor.query.characterLimit()
```

`characterLimit()` returns `null` when there is no limit. The package also exports `countCharacters(node)`, which counts the characters in a ProseMirror node with the same rules.

## Does the one-script build have a character limit?

No. The character count extension is not part of the one-script build; add it with the npm package.

## What happens if I load text that is over the limit?

Content you load yourself is not cut. The writer can delete and edit, but changes that add characters are refused until the text is below the limit.

## Do spaces count?

Yes. Every character in the text counts, spaces included. Images, videos and line breaks do not.

---

# Open, save and print

> Use the File menu to open Word, Markdown, HTML and text files, save as Word, Markdown or HTML, and print the document.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

The toolbar has a File menu. It opens `.docx`, `.md`, `.html` and `.txt` files, saves the text as Word, Markdown or HTML, and prints it (choose "Save as PDF" in the print dialog for a PDF). This page covers turning the menu on and off, loading the converters, and what Word and Markdown files keep and drop.

## The File menu

The menu holds: "Open file…", "Save as Word (.docx)", "Save as Markdown (.md)", "Save as HTML (.html)" and "Print or PDF".

- An opened file replaces an empty document. If there is text, the file goes in at the cursor. One undo takes it back.
- In text files, blank lines separate paragraphs and single line breaks stay as line breaks.
- Every opened file goes through the same document rules as pasted content, so unknown markup never reaches the output. Sanitize the saved HTML on the server as well.
- Saved files are named from the `fileName` option ("document" if not set). Characters that file names cannot hold are replaced, and the name is at most 100 characters.
- Errors appear in a visible notice. Progress messages such as "Opening file…" are announced to screen readers.

## With the one-script build

The menu is there by default, with the Word and Markdown converters. The converters live in two extra files next to the main script and load on first use. To hide the menu for one textarea, add `data-files="false"`:

```html
<textarea name="body" data-editor data-files="false"></textarea>
```

For the add-on addresses, the fingerprint check and Content Security Policy settings, see [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/).

## With npm

Pass the converters as loader functions, so they download only when used:

```ts
import { createUI } from '@viveeditor/ui'

createUI(editor, {
  files: {
    docx: () => import('@viveeditor/docx'),
    markdown: () => import('@viveeditor/markdown'),
    upload,
    fileName: 'Report',
  },
})
```

In the framework components, pass the same object inside `ui: { files: { … } }`; the components add no loaders by default.

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `docx` | A loader that returns the `@viveeditor/docx` module. Turns on opening and saving Word files. |
| `markdown` | A loader that returns the `@viveeditor/markdown` module. Turns on opening and saving Markdown. |
| `html` | `false` removes saving as HTML. |
| `print` | `false` removes printing. |
| `fileName` | The name of saved files. |
| `upload` | The function that uploads images from Word files to your server. It follows the same contract as the upload function in [Images and uploads](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/images-and-uploads/). |
| `allowBase64` | Embeds images from Word files in the document instead of uploading them. |

Without loaders, the menu opens HTML and text files, saves as HTML and prints. `files: false` hides the menu.

## Limits

- Word files can be up to 20 MB; HTML, Markdown and text files up to 5 MB. The Markdown converter handles up to 1 MB of text.
- Password-protected files and files that unpack too large or too deep are refused with a message.
- `.doc`, `.odt` and `.rtf` are not supported.
- If some images in a Word file cannot be added, the menu says how many. If other unsupported content was left out, it says so too.

## Printing

"Print or PDF" opens the browser's print dialog. The document is prepared in a hidden frame that runs no scripts and loads only images and styles. Video players print as links.

For your own button, call `printDocument(editor, { title, css })` from `@viveeditor/ui`.

## Markdown

Headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, links, images, bullet, numbered and nested lists, checklists, quotes, rules, fenced code with its language and tables are read and written.

Markdown has no form for text colour, highlight, underline and alignment, so they are left out when saving. Video players are saved as links. Raw HTML inside Markdown is never let through.

## Word (.docx)

| Kept when opening and saving | Left out |
| --- | --- |
| Headings (a Word title opens as a level 1 heading), bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, text colour, highlight, alignment | Comments, footnotes, headers and footers, text boxes, equations |
| Bullet, numbered and nested lists | Tracked deletions (insertions are kept), hidden text |
| Links to web and mail addresses | Other links become plain text; field codes keep only their visible text |
| Tables with merged cells and header rows, quotes, code | Code block language |
| Images (opening needs your upload function or `allowBase64`) | Without one, images are dropped and the menu says how many |

Checklists are saved as ☐ and ☑ text and video players as links. The saved file uses A4 pages and carries no author.

> **Images saved to Word**
>
> Images stored as data addresses are embedded in the file. Images at web addresses are downloaded and embedded only when you call `exportDocx` yourself with `fetchImages: true`; the File menu does not, and writes those images as links.

## Use the converters directly

You can convert without the menu:

```ts
import { exportDocx, importDocx } from '@viveeditor/docx'
import { markdownToHtml, toMarkdown } from '@viveeditor/markdown'

const { html, warnings } = await importDocx(file, { upload })
editor.commands.replaceContent(html)

const blob = await exportDocx(editor, { title: 'Report' })

editor.commands.replaceContent(markdownToHtml('# Title\n\nSome **bold** text'))
const markdown = toMarkdown(editor)
```

For files it refuses, `importDocx` throws a `DocxError` with the code `TOO_LARGE`, `NOT_DOCX`, `ENCRYPTED`, `UNSUPPORTED`, `DAMAGED`, `TOO_COMPLEX` or `ABORTED`. `warnings` lists left-out content as `{ code, count }`.

To format pasted Markdown text, see `MarkdownPaste` on the [Paste from Office](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/paste-from-office/) page.

## How do I save as PDF?

Choose "Print or PDF" from the File menu, then pick "Save as PDF" in the browser's print dialog.

## Can I open .doc, .odt or .rtf files?

No. Only .docx, .md, .html, .htm and .txt files open. Save older files as .docx in Word or LibreOffice first.

## Does an opened file replace my text?

If the document is empty, the file replaces it. If there is text, the file goes in at the cursor. Either way, one undo takes it back.

---

# Paste from Office

> Clean paste from Word, Google Docs and LibreOffice; fake bullets become real lists, and pasted Markdown text becomes formatted content.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/paste-from-office/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

`@viveeditor/ext-office-paste` cleans content pasted from Word, Google Docs and LibreOffice. It turns Word's fake bullets and numbers into real nested lists, keeps Word's title and quote styles and fixes lists that Google Docs nests the wrong way. This page also covers `MarkdownPaste`, which turns Markdown pasted as plain text into formatted content.

## Setup

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import { OfficePaste } from '@viveeditor/ext-office-paste'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [
    OfficePaste.configure({ onDropped: ({ images }) => console.warn(`${images} images left out`) }),
  ],
})
```

The one-script build already includes the extension. Its only option is `onDropped`.

## What gets fixed

In content from Word:

- Word's lists are not real lists but paragraphs with markers. These paragraphs become real, nested bulleted and numbered lists. The list type and start number come from Word's list definition, or from the marker itself.
- Marker characters are removed everywhere.
- Word's Title style becomes a level 1 heading, and its Quote style becomes a quote.

From every source:

- A sub-list sitting directly inside a list moves into the item above it. Google Docs copies lists this way.
- Text that is both underlined and struck through keeps both.
- Images that point at files on the copying computer (`file:` and `blob:` addresses) are left out and counted.

HTML that does not come from Word, Google Docs or LibreOffice passes through this extension unchanged. Every paste, whatever its source, then goes through the document rules, so unknown markup never reaches the output.

## Left-out images

Images that point at files on the copying computer cannot be pasted. When images are left out, `onDropped` is called with:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `source` | `'word'`, `'docs'` or `'libreoffice'` |
| `images` | The number of images left out |

Use it to show the writer a message asking them to upload those images separately. For image uploads, see [Images and uploads](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/images-and-uploads/).

## Helper functions

To run the same cleaning outside paste, the package exports three functions:

| Function | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `detectOffice(html)` | `'word'`, `'docs'`, `'libreoffice'` or `null` |
| `cleanOffice(html)` | `{ html, source, droppedImages }` |
| `cleanOfficeHtml(html)` | Only the cleaned HTML |

## Markdown paste

`MarkdownPaste` from `@viveeditor/markdown/paste` turns Markdown pasted as plain text into formatted content. The converter loads only when needed:

```ts
import { MarkdownPaste } from '@viveeditor/markdown/paste'

const markdownPaste = MarkdownPaste.configure({ load: () => import('@viveeditor/markdown') })
```

It converts only when:

- the clipboard holds plain text and no HTML,
- the text looks like Markdown: it has a heading, fenced code, a quote, a table, bold text, a link, a checklist item or at least two list lines,
- the cursor is not in a code block.

If the converter fails to load, the text is pasted as plain text. Text longer than one million characters is not converted. Raw HTML inside Markdown is never let through. To check in advance whether text would be converted, use `looksLikeMarkdown(text)` from the same package.

Markdown paste is on in the one-script CDN version; the converter loads from the add-on file on first use. To open and save Markdown files, see [Open, save and print](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/).

## Why are images pasted from Word missing?

Word puts some images on the clipboard as addresses of files on the copying computer. The browser cannot read those, so they are left out; onDropped tells you how many.

## Is Office paste on in the one-script build?

Yes. The Office paste extension is loaded by default in the one-script build, and Markdown paste is on in the CDN version.

## When does Markdown paste kick in?

Only when the clipboard has no HTML and the plain text looks like Markdown. Text pasted inside a code block is never converted.

---

# Mentions

> Add @mentions with the Mention extension and mentionMenu, store checked ids, and verify every mention again on your server.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/mentions/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

Mentions let a writer type `@` and pick a person, a team or any other entry from a list you supply. The editor stores an opaque id and a plain-text label. Your server decides who the id really is, who may be mentioned and who gets notified.

Mentions ship as npm packages only. The one-script build does not include them.

## Set it up

1. Install the extension and the UI: `npm install @viveeditor/ext-mention @viveeditor/ui @viveeditor/core`.
2. Add `Mention` to the editor's extensions.
3. Add `mentionMenu` from `@viveeditor/ui/extras` to the `plugins` of `createUI`, with an `items` function that returns matching entries.

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import { basicExtensions } from '@viveeditor/ext-basic'
import { Mention } from '@viveeditor/ext-mention'
import { createUI } from '@viveeditor/ui'
import { mentionMenu } from '@viveeditor/ui/extras'
import '@viveeditor/ext-mention/style.css'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [...basicExtensions, Mention],
})

createUI(editor, {
  plugins: [
    mentionMenu({
      items: async (query, signal) => {
        const response = await fetch(`/mentions?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`, { signal })
        if (!response.ok) return []
        return response.json()
      },
    }),
  ],
})
```

`/mentions` stands for your own search endpoint. Each entry you return has an `id`, a `label` and an optional `description`.

## How the menu behaves

- The menu opens when the writer types `@` at the start of a line or after a space. The query is up to 32 letters, digits, `_`, `.` or `-`.
- Your `items` function runs 150 ms after the last keystroke. When the writer keeps typing or closes the menu, the `signal` is aborted, so pass it to `fetch`.
- The menu shows at most 8 entries, as plain text. Your labels are never read as HTML.
- `Enter` or `Tab` picks an entry and `Esc` closes the menu.

You can also insert a mention from code with `editor.commands.insertMention({ id: 'u_42', label: 'Editor' })`.

## What is stored

A mention is saved as one span:

```html
<span class="vive-mention" data-mention="u_42">@Editor</span>
```

The id must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.:@-]{0,127}$` and must not contain `..`. The pattern is exported as `MENTION_ID_PATTERN`, and `isMentionId()` tests a value against it. The editor checks the id when it reads HTML, when it reads JSON and when it writes HTML. A span whose id fails the check is not read as a mention.

The label loses control, bidi and zero-width characters and is capped at 100 characters. The `maxLabelLength` option of `Mention` changes the cap. An id never becomes a link address.

## Check mentions on the server

The browser is not a security boundary. Anyone can post a span with any id and any label. When you save the content:

- clean the HTML with [the server sanitizer](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/). It keeps mentions in exactly the form above and reduces a mention with a bad id, or one placed inside a link or a footnote, to its text;
- look every id up in your own directory and drop the ones that do not exist;
- check that the writer may mention that person or group;
- build the displayed name from your own data, not from the stored label;
- keep ids opaque. Do not use e-mail addresses or other personal data as ids.

The search endpoint behind `items` needs authentication, a rate limit and tenant scoping, so a writer only finds people they are allowed to see.

## Notifications

viveEditor sends no notifications. If you notify people who were mentioned:

- compare the ids before and after an edit and notify only new mentions;
- deduplicate, so one person mentioned five times gets one notice;
- rate-limit the notices you send per writer.

## Related pages

- [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/)
- [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/)
- [Packages](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/packages/)

## Where does the list of people come from?

From your own items function. viveEditor has no user directory; it calls your function with the typed text and an AbortSignal and shows what you return.

## Can I trust the name stored in a mention?

No. The label is whatever the writer's browser sent. Look the id up in your own directory and build the displayed name from your data.

---

# Emoji

> Add an emoji picker that opens on a colon, with a compact English emoji list that loads only on first use.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/emoji/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

The emoji menu lets a writer type `:` and two letters, then pick an emoji by name or keyword. The emoji goes into the text as an ordinary character, so the stored HTML needs no extra element and the menu needs no editor extension.

The emoji menu ships as an npm package only. The one-script build does not include it.

## Set it up

1. Install the UI and the data: `npm install @viveeditor/ui @viveeditor/emoji-data`.
2. Add `emojiMenu` from `@viveeditor/ui/extras` to the `plugins` of `createUI`.
3. Pass a `load` function that imports the list, so it downloads only when needed.

```ts
import { createUI } from '@viveeditor/ui'
import { emojiMenu } from '@viveeditor/ui/extras'

createUI(editor, {
  plugins: [emojiMenu({ load: () => import('@viveeditor/emoji-data/en') })],
})
```

## How the menu behaves

- The menu opens when the writer types `:` at the start of a line or after a space, followed by at least two letters or digits.
- It searches names and keywords. An exact name comes first, then names that start with the typed text, then keyword matches.
- It shows at most 8 results. `Enter` or `Tab` inserts the emoji and `Esc` closes the menu.
- The list loads once, on first use. If loading fails, the next attempt tries again.

## The data package

`@viveeditor/emoji-data/en` is a compact English list of about 39 KB. It is generated from [emojibase-data](https://www.npmjs.com/package/emojibase-data) 18.0.0 and only English names are available.

Each row has three parts: the emoji, its name and its keywords. The menu checks the list when it loads. It refuses a list with more than 5,000 rows, or a row in another shape, and an emoji longer than 16 code points.

## Your own list

`load` can return any list in the same shape, as an array or as a module with a `default` export. Use this for a shorter list or for names in another language.

```ts
import { type EmojiRow, emojiMenu } from '@viveeditor/ui/extras'

const rows: EmojiRow[] = [
  ['👍', 'thumbs up', ['yes', 'agree']],
  ['🎉', 'party popper', ['celebrate']],
]

emojiMenu({ load: async () => rows })
```

## Licence

The package itself is MIT licensed. The emoji names and keywords come from Emojibase, which is under the MIT License, and Emojibase derives them from the Unicode CLDR and the Unicode emoji data files, under the Unicode License v3. The `NOTICE` file in the package holds both notices. Keep it when you redistribute the data.

## Related pages

- [Packages](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/packages/)
- [Mentions](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/mentions/)

## Does the emoji list load with the editor?

No. The list loads the first time a writer types a colon and two letters, so pages that never use it do not download it.

## Can I use my own emoji list?

Yes. The load function can return any list of rows in the form emoji, name, keywords, up to 5,000 rows.

---

# Formulas (LaTeX)

> Write LaTeX formulas with MathExtension and your own KaTeX 0.18.2 or newer, then draw them on published pages with renderMath.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/formulas/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

The formula extension lets writers type LaTeX and see it drawn by [KaTeX](https://katex.org) while they edit. The editor stores only the LaTeX source, never the drawing, so the saved HTML stays small and clean. On the published page you draw the formulas again with `renderMath`.

Formulas ship as npm packages only. The one-script build does not include them.

## Set it up

1. Install the extension, the UI and KaTeX: `npm install @viveeditor/ext-math @viveeditor/ui @viveeditor/core katex`.
2. Add `MathExtension` with a `load` function that imports KaTeX. KaTeX then downloads only when a formula is shown.
3. Import KaTeX's stylesheet and the extension's stylesheet.
4. Add `mathTools()` to the `plugins` of `createUI` for the `/` menu entries.

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import { basicExtensions } from '@viveeditor/ext-basic'
import { MathExtension } from '@viveeditor/ext-math'
import { createUI } from '@viveeditor/ui'
```
