```ts
import { mathTools } from '@viveeditor/ui/extras'
import '@viveeditor/ext-math/style.css'
import 'katex/dist/katex.min.css'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [
    ...basicExtensions,
    MathExtension.configure({
      load: () => import('katex'),
      onError: (error) => console.warn(error.code, error.version),
    }),
  ],
})

createUI(editor, { plugins: [mathTools()] })
```

## KaTeX version

KaTeX must be **0.18.2 or newer** (`MIN_KATEX_VERSION`). The floor follows the KaTeX security advisory GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7. An older version is refused and the formula's source is shown instead of a drawing.

`onError` receives an error with one of two codes:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `KATEX_OUTDATED` | The loaded KaTeX is older than 0.18.2; `version` holds its version. |
| `KATEX_LOAD` | The `load` function failed. |

The editor passes fixed options to KaTeX, including `trust: false`, so a formula cannot add links or other HTML.

## Writing formulas

- **Inline:** type `$x^2$`. When you type the closing `$`, the text between the dollars becomes a formula. It must not start or end with a space.
- **Block:** type `$$` on an empty line and press `Enter`.
- **Menu:** pick "Formula" or "Block formula" from the `/` menu. These entries come from `mathTools()`.
- **Edit:** click a formula, or select it and press `Enter`, to edit its source with a live preview. `Enter` finishes an inline formula, `Ctrl+Enter` (`⌘+Enter` on a Mac) finishes a block formula, and `Esc` leaves without changes.

From code, `editor.commands.insertMath({ display: true, latex: 'E = mc^2' })` inserts a block formula. Leave out `display` for an inline one.

A formula holds at most 2,000 characters (`MAX_LATEX_LENGTH`) and at most 64 levels of nested braces.

## What is stored

```html
<p>Area: <span data-math="inline">\pi r^2</span></p>
<div data-math="block">\int_0^1 x\,dx</div>
```

[The server sanitizer](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/) keeps formulas in exactly this form. A formula that fails its check, or one placed inside a link or a footnote, is reduced to its text.

When the text is saved as Markdown, formulas are written as `$…$` and `$$` blocks. When it is saved as Word, the LaTeX source is written in a code font.

## Published pages

Call `renderMath` on the element that holds the content. It loads KaTeX the same way and returns the number of formulas it drew. The page needs KaTeX's stylesheet too.

```ts
import { renderMath } from '@viveeditor/ext-math/render'
import 'katex/dist/katex.min.css'

const article = document.querySelector('article')
if (article) await renderMath(article, { load: () => import('katex') })
```

- It draws at most 1,000 formulas per call, in batches, so long pages stay responsive.
- Formulas already drawn are skipped, so calling it again is safe.
- Each drawn formula gets its LaTeX source as `aria-label`.

## Related pages

- [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/)
- [Footnotes](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/footnotes/)
- [Open, save and print](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/)

## Does viveEditor include KaTeX?

No. KaTeX is your own dependency. You pass a load function, and the editor refuses versions older than 0.18.2.

## Is the drawn formula saved?

No. Only the LaTeX source is stored. Published pages draw it again with renderMath.

---

# Footnotes

> Add footnotes that writers edit in place, then number them and list them at the end of published pages with renderFootnotes.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/footnotes/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

The footnote extension lets a writer add a note at any point in the text and type it right there, without jumping to the end of the page. The note is stored where it belongs in the sentence. On the published page `renderFootnotes` numbers the notes and lists them at the end.

Footnotes ship as npm packages only. The one-script build does not include them.

## Set it up

1. Install the extension and the UI: `npm install @viveeditor/ext-footnote @viveeditor/ui @viveeditor/core`.
2. Add `Footnote` to the editor's extensions and import its stylesheet.
3. Add `footnoteTools()` to the `plugins` of `createUI` for the `/` menu entry.

```ts
import { Editor } from '@viveeditor/core'
import { basicExtensions } from '@viveeditor/ext-basic'
import { Footnote } from '@viveeditor/ext-footnote'
import { createUI } from '@viveeditor/ui'
import { footnoteTools } from '@viveeditor/ui/extras'
import '@viveeditor/ext-footnote/style.css'

const editor = await Editor.create(document.querySelector('#editor'), {
  extensions: [...basicExtensions, Footnote],
})

createUI(editor, { plugins: [footnoteTools()] })
```

## Writing footnotes

- Pick "Footnote" from the `/` menu. A numbered marker appears at the cursor and a small box opens under it.
- Type the note in the box. `Enter` or `Esc` returns to the main text.
- Select the marker again to edit the note.

From code, `editor.commands.insertFootnote()` inserts an empty note at the cursor.

Notes keep bold, italic and links only. Other formatting is removed, and a note cannot sit inside a link. A note holds at most 5,000 characters (`MAX_FOOTNOTE_LENGTH`). Inside the editor the markers are numbered in order as you write.

## What is stored

```html
<p>The study ran for two years.<sup data-footnote="">Results were published in <em>2025</em>.</sup></p>
```

[The server sanitizer](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/) keeps footnotes in exactly this form. Inside a footnote only text, bold, italic and links survive. A footnote, mention or formula nested where it cannot live is reduced to its text.

## Published pages

Call `renderFootnotes` on the element that holds the content:

```ts
import { renderFootnotes } from '@viveeditor/ext-footnote/render'

const article = document.querySelector('article')
if (article) renderFootnotes(article, { backLabel: 'Back to text' })
```

- Each note in the text becomes a number that links to its entry.
- The notes are listed in an `<ol class="vive-footnotes">` appended to the end of that element.
- Each entry gets a ↩ link back to its place in the text. `backLabel` is its accessible name and defaults to "Back to text".
- A note that sits inside a link becomes a plain number, without a link of its own.
- Notes already handled are skipped, so calling it again is safe. It returns the number of notes it handled.

## Printing and saving

When the writer prints from the File menu, the notes are numbered and listed at the end of the printed page in the same way.

Saving as Markdown writes footnotes as `[^n]` with the definitions at the end. Saving as Word writes superscript numbers with the notes at the end. Opening a Word file does not bring its footnotes in.

## Related pages

- [Open, save and print](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/)
- [Formulas](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/formulas/)
- [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/)

## Are footnote numbers stored in the HTML?

No. The note text is stored where it belongs in the sentence. Numbers are added by renderFootnotes on the published page and by printing.

## What formatting can a footnote hold?

Bold, italic and links only. Other formatting is removed.

---

# Templates

> Offer ready-made content blocks in the slash menu with templateMenu; every template goes through the editor schema before it lands.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/templates/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

Templates give writers a quick start: a memo layout, a meeting note, a product page skeleton. `templateMenu` adds one entry per template to the `/` menu, and picking it inserts the template's content at the cursor.

Templates ship as an npm package only. The one-script build does not include them.

## Set it up

1. Install the UI: `npm install @viveeditor/ui @viveeditor/core`.
2. Write your templates as a list of entries.
3. Pass the list to `templateMenu` and add it to the `plugins` of `createUI`.

```ts
import { createUI } from '@viveeditor/ui'
import { type Template, templateMenu } from '@viveeditor/ui/extras'

const templates: Template[] = [
  {
    id: 'memo',
    label: 'Memo',
    description: 'Subject, summary and next steps',
    content: '<h2>Subject</h2><p></p><h3>Next steps</h3><ul><li><p></p></li></ul>',
  },
  {
    id: 'meeting',
    label: 'Meeting notes',
    content: '<h2>Meeting notes</h2><p><strong>Attendees:</strong> </p><p></p>',
  },
]

createUI(editor, { plugins: [templateMenu(templates)] })
```

## Template entries

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | A unique name for the entry. |
| `label` | The text shown in the `/` menu, after "Template:". |
| `description` | Optional. Extra words the menu search matches. |
| `content` | The content to insert, as an HTML string or as editor JSON. |

The menu search also matches the label and the words "template" and "sablon". The second argument of `templateMenu` overrides menu labels, for example `templateMenu(templates, { template: 'Layout' })`.

When the editor is read-only, picking a template inserts nothing.

## Schema filtering

Template content goes through the editor schema, the same way as pasted content. Anything the schema does not know is dropped: scripts, event handlers, unknown elements and attributes. A template can only use the blocks and formatting the editor has extensions for. If a template has a table but the table extension is not loaded, it is not kept as a table.

## Size limit

A template whose HTML is over 2 MB is skipped and does not appear in the menu.

## Trust

The schema removes unsafe markup, but it cannot judge the words and links in a template. Only offer templates you wrote or trust. If writers can create templates for each other, store them through [the server sanitizer](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/) and check who may publish a template for whom.

## Related pages

- [Toolbar and shortcuts](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/toolbar-and-shortcuts/)
- [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/)

## Can a template carry scripts or custom markup?

No. Template content goes through the editor schema like pasted content, so scripts and unknown markup are dropped.

## Is there a size limit?

Yes. Templates over 2 MB are skipped and do not appear in the menu.

---

# AI assistant

> Connect the AI assistant to your own server through a provider function; answers are shown and inserted as plain text.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/ai-assistant/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

The AI assistant gives writers actions such as "Improve writing" or "Summarize" on selected text. viveEditor provides the panel and the rules for showing and inserting answers. It sends nothing anywhere itself: you pass a provider function that calls your own server, and your server talks to the AI service.

The AI assistant ships as an npm package only. The one-script build does not include it.

## Set it up

1. Install the UI: `npm install @viveeditor/ui @viveeditor/core`.
2. Write a `generate` function that sends the request to your own endpoint.
3. Add `aiAssistant` to the `plugins` of `createUI`.

```ts
import { createUI } from '@viveeditor/ui'
import { type AiRequest, aiAssistant } from '@viveeditor/ui/extras'

async function generate(request: AiRequest): Promise<string> {
  const response = await fetch('/ai', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-CSRF-Token': csrfToken },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      action: request.action,
      instruction: request.instruction,
      text: request.text,
      context: request.context,
      locale: request.locale,
    }),
    signal: request.signal,
  })
  if (!response.ok) throw new Error('AI request failed')
  const { text } = await response.json()
  return text
}

createUI(editor, { plugins: [aiAssistant({ provider: { generate } })] })
```

`/ai` is a placeholder for your own endpoint, and `csrfToken` is the token your site already uses. The response shape is up to you.

## Opening the assistant

- Select text and press the AI button in the selection bubble.
- Press `Ctrl+J` (`⌘+J` on a Mac).
- Type `/ai` and pick "AI" from the `/` menu.

The panel lists the actions, a field for a custom instruction and, once an answer arrives, the buttons Replace selection, Insert below, Try again and Discard. Stop ends a running request and `Esc` closes the panel.

## The provider contract

`provider.generate(request)` returns either a promise of a string or an async iterable of strings. Return an async iterable to stream the answer as it arrives.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `action` | `improve`, `fix`, `shorten`, `expand`, `tone`, `translate`, `summarize`, `continue`, or `custom` for a typed instruction. |
| `instruction` | The writer's own instruction, only for `custom`. |
| `text` | The selected text. |
| `context` | `before` and `after`: up to 2,000 characters of text on each side of the selection. |
| `locale` | The editor's language, `tr` or `en`. |
| `signal` | An `AbortSignal`. Pass it to `fetch`; it fires when the writer stops, closes the panel or the time limit is reached. |

The `actions` option chooses which actions the panel shows and in what order, for example `actions: ['fix', 'shorten', 'summarize']`. "Continue writing" and a custom instruction work without a selection; the other actions need selected text.

A streaming provider can read the response body piece by piece:

```ts
import type { AiRequest } from '@viveeditor/ui/extras'

async function* stream(request: AiRequest): AsyncIterable<string> {
  const response = await fetch('/ai', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-CSRF-Token': csrfToken },
    body: JSON.stringify({ action: request.action, text: request.text }),
    signal: request.signal,
  })
  if (!response.ok || !response.body) throw new Error('AI request failed')
  const reader = response.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader()
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read()
    if (done) return
    yield value
  }
}
```

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Selected text | 20,000 characters; a longer selection is not sent and the panel asks for a shorter one |
| Context | 2,000 characters on each side |
| Custom instruction | 1,000 characters |
| Answer | 20,000 characters; the rest is cut off |
| Time | 2 minutes per request, then it is stopped |

Only one request runs at a time. Starting a new one cancels the last, and pieces that arrive late are dropped.

## How answers are inserted

The AI answer is untrusted text. It is shown in the panel as plain text and inserted as plain paragraphs, never as HTML. Nothing changes in the document until the writer picks Replace selection or Insert below, and one undo removes it. If the selected text changed while the answer was being written, Replace selection is turned off and the answer can only be inserted below.

If you want headings and lists from the answer, the `markdown` option takes a loader for a Markdown renderer. Its HTML loses images, media and scripts, and also links unless you pass `links: true`, and then goes through the editor schema:

```ts
import { aiAssistant } from '@viveeditor/ui/extras'

aiAssistant({
  provider: { generate },
  markdown: async () => (await import('@viveeditor/markdown')).markdownToHtml,
})
```

## AI server checklist

The provider should call your own endpoint, never an AI vendor directly from the browser.

- Keep the API key on the server. Require a signed-in session and a CSRF token.
- Fix the system prompt, the model and `max_tokens` on the server. Accept only the actions you allow and limit the input size again.
- Set a quota and rate limit per user, and a spending cap at the AI vendor.
- Keep document text out of your logs, or mask it. Tell writers that their text is sent to a third party, as your privacy rules (KVKK, GDPR) require.
- If you later give the model tools or retrieval, prompt injection from the document becomes a serious risk; review that design separately.

## Related pages

- [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/)
- [Toolbar and shortcuts](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/toolbar-and-shortcuts/)

## Which AI service does viveEditor use?

None. viveEditor sends nothing anywhere itself. Your provider function decides where the request goes, and it should go to your own server.

## Can the AI answer change the document without the writer?

No. The answer is shown first, and nothing is applied until the writer chooses Replace selection or Insert below. One undo removes it.

---

# Server sanitizing

> Clean posted HTML on your server with @viveeditor/sanitize for Node or viveeditor/sanitizer for PHP 8.4+, on save and on print.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

The editor only produces a known set of HTML, but anyone can post any HTML to your server. Clean it there before you store or show it. `@viveeditor/sanitize` for Node and `viveeditor/sanitizer` for PHP 8.4+ keep exactly what the editor produces and remove everything else. They share one allowlist and one test corpus and give the same output.

## Install

For Node.js 20.19 or newer:

```sh
npm install @viveeditor/sanitize
```

For PHP 8.4 or newer, with the `dom` and `mbstring` extensions and no other dependencies:

```sh
composer require viveeditor/sanitizer
```

On Laravel, use [viveeditor/laravel](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/laravel/), which brings the PHP sanitizer with it.

## Clean the HTML

```ts
import { sanitizeHtml } from '@viveeditor/sanitize'

const clean = sanitizeHtml(request.body.html, { embeds: true })
```

```php
use Viveeditor\Sanitizer\Sanitizer;

$clean = Sanitizer::sanitize($html, ['embeds' => true]);
```

Every element and attribute is rebuilt with a full HTML5 parser (`parse5` in Node, `Dom\HTMLDocument` in PHP), so the output reads the same way in every browser. Cleaning twice gives the same result.

## Options

| Option | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `embeds` | `false` | Keeps video and audio embeds. Players are rebuilt from the provider and id, never copied. |
| `allowBase64` | `false` | Allows images stored as `data:` addresses (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF). |
| `allowRelativeImages` | `false` | Allows relative image addresses. |
| `maxBytes` | 2 MB | HTML larger than this throws `TOO_LARGE`. |

Turn `allowRelativeImages` on only if you need it: a relative image address makes every reader's browser send a GET request to your own site, which a writer could aim at an address that changes something.

## Errors

The sanitizer never cuts HTML short. When it cannot clean the input, it throws:

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `TOO_LARGE` | The HTML is larger than `maxBytes`. |
| `TOO_COMPLEX` | The structure would make the parser slow or memory hungry: more than 64 attributes on one tag, nesting deeper than 512 levels, or far more elements than the input has tags. The editor never writes such HTML. |

In Node the error is a `SanitizeError` with a `code`:

```ts
import { SanitizeError, sanitizeHtml } from '@viveeditor/sanitize'

export function cleanArticle(html: string): string | null {
  try {
    return sanitizeHtml(html)
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof SanitizeError) return null
    throw error
  }
}
```

In PHP it is a `SanitizeException` whose `reason` is `SanitizeException::TOO_LARGE` or `SanitizeException::TOO_COMPLEX`:

```php
use Viveeditor\Sanitizer\SanitizeException;
use Viveeditor\Sanitizer\Sanitizer;

try {
    $clean = Sanitizer::sanitize($html);
} catch (SanitizeException $error) {
    $clean = null;
    $reason = $error->reason;
}
```

## What is kept

- **Links** keep `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `tel` and relative addresses, and always get `rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"`.
- **Images** need `https` addresses. `allowBase64` and `allowRelativeImages` widen that.
- **Embeds** are removed unless you pass `embeds: true`.
- **`style`** keeps only text alignment, text and highlight colour, and table widths.
- **`id`, `name`, `form` and event handlers** never pass.
- **Scripts, styles, frames, SVG and similar elements** are removed together with their content.
- **Mentions, formulas and footnotes** are kept in exactly the form the editor writes them. A mention id or formula that fails its check, or one placed inside a link or a footnote, is reduced to its text. Footnotes keep only bold, italic and links.

## PHP memory note

In PHP the parser cannot be stopped from inside, so some short hostile inputs (a few tens of KB of unclosed formatting tags) can reach PHP's `memory_limit` before the check runs. PHP then ends that request with a fatal error, which is safe but not a clean exception.

Keep `memory_limit` and `max_execution_time` at their usual values for the endpoints that sanitize, and limit the request body size there.

## When to clean

1. **On save.** Clean the posted HTML before you store it.
2. **On print.** Show stored HTML through a cleaning helper too (`@viveHtml` in Laravel). Rows written before you added cleaning, or written outside your forms, then stay safe.

> **Never print raw HTML**
>
> Do not print stored HTML unescaped without cleaning it, even if it was cleaned once on save.

## Related pages

- [Laravel](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/laravel/)
- [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/)
- [Images and uploads](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/images-and-uploads/)
- [Video embeds](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/video-embeds/)

## The editor already produces clean HTML. Why clean it again on the server?

Because anyone can post any HTML to your server without using the editor. The browser is not a security boundary.

## Do the Node and PHP sanitizers give the same result?

Yes. They share one allowlist and one test corpus and give the same output.

## What happens when the HTML is too large?

The sanitizer throws a TOO_LARGE error instead of cutting the HTML. The default limit is 2 MB.

---

# Laravel

> Add viveEditor to Laravel with a Blade component, local editor files, the @viveHtml directive and the ViveHtml cast for clean HTML.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/laravel/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

`viveeditor/laravel` brings viveEditor to Laravel 12 and newer on PHP 8.4 and newer. It adds a Blade component for the editor, serves the editor files from your own site and cleans HTML with [the PHP sanitizer](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/) when you save it and when you show it.

## Install

1. Add the package: `composer require viveeditor/laravel`. Laravel finds the service provider and the `ViveEditor` facade on its own.
2. Publish the editor files to `public/vendor/viveeditor`: `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=viveeditor-assets`.
3. Optionally publish the config file: `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=viveeditor-config`.

```sh
composer require viveeditor/laravel
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=viveeditor-assets
```

The editor files are published as copies. After you update the package, publish them again with `--force` so they match the new version. They are also tagged `laravel-assets`.

## Show the editor

Put `@viveeditorScripts` in the page's `<head>`. It prints the stylesheet and the editor script from your own `public/vendor/viveeditor`. Then use the component inside your form:

```blade
<head>
  @viveeditorScripts
</head>

<form method="post">
  @csrf
  <label for="body">Article</label>
  <x-viveeditor::editor name="body" id="body" :value="old('body', $post->body)" required />
  <button type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
```

The component renders a `<textarea>` that the editor takes over. The form posts the HTML under the field's `name`.

| Attribute | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Required. The form field name. |
| `value` | The starting HTML. Escaped for you. |
| `label` | Optional. Becomes the field's `aria-label` when there is no visible `<label>`. |

Other attributes, such as `id`, `required` or `data-files="false"` to hide the File menu, are passed to the textarea.

The component uses the one-script build, so the npm-only extras (mentions, emoji, formulas, footnotes, templates and the AI assistant) are not part of it.

## Show stored HTML

Print stored HTML with `@viveHtml(...)`. It cleans while printing, so rows written before you added cleaning, and rows written outside your forms, are safe too.

```blade
<article>@viveHtml($post->body)</article>
```

> **Never use the unescaped echo**
>
> Never print editor HTML with `{!! !!}`. It skips cleaning.

## Clean on save

The `ViveHtml` cast cleans on save and again on read, so rows written before the cast or by raw queries come back clean.

```php
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Viveeditor\Laravel\Casts\ViveHtml;

class Post extends Model
{
    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return ['body' => ViveHtml::class];
    }
}
```

A row the cast cannot clean on read (too large or too complex) reads as an empty string, and the error goes to your exception handler. On save the error is thrown.

To clean anywhere else, use the facade. The second argument overrides the config options for that call:

```php
use Viveeditor\Laravel\Facades\ViveEditor;

$clean = ViveEditor::sanitize($request->input('body'));
$withEmbeds = ViveEditor::sanitize($html, ['embeds' => true]);
```

`ViveEditor::sanitize()` and `@viveHtml` throw `Viveeditor\Sanitizer\SanitizeException` for HTML that is too large or too complex. See [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/) for the limits.

## Configuration

`config/viveeditor.php` holds the asset folder and the sanitizer options used by `@viveHtml`, the cast and the facade:

```php
return [

    'asset_path' => env('VIVEEDITOR_ASSET_PATH', 'vendor/viveeditor'),

    'sanitize' => [
        'embeds' => false,
        'allowBase64' => false,
        'allowRelativeImages' => false,
    ],

];
```

If you enable video embeds in the editor, set `embeds` to `true` here, or they are removed when the HTML is cleaned.

## Content Security Policy

When you use `Vite::useCspNonce()`, the tags printed by `@viveeditorScripts` get the nonce. The editor copies that nonce to the add-on scripts it loads on first use (the Word and Markdown converters and the panels), which sit in the same folder. Your `script-src` must allow that folder. See [Laravel's Vite documentation](https://laravel.com/docs/vite) for setting the nonce, and [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/) for the rest of the policy.

## Language

The editor follows `<html lang="...">` for its language. Set it from the app locale in your layout:

```blade
<html lang="{{ str_replace('_', '-', app()->getLocale()) }}">
```

## Related pages

- [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/)
- [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/)
- [Installation](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/)

## Does the Laravel package load anything from a CDN?

No. The editor files are published to your own public/vendor/viveeditor folder and served from there.

## Can I print stored HTML with the unescaped Blade echo?

No. Show stored HTML with @viveHtml, which cleans it while printing, so old rows and rows written outside your forms are safe too.

---

# Packages

> Every viveEditor package, what it does, which entry points it has and where its public API report lives.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/packages/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

viveEditor is split into small packages so you load only what you use. This page lists every package, what it does and its extra entry points. The public API of each npm package is recorded in the [`api/` folder](https://github.com/mtvrkan/viveeditor/tree/main/api) of the repository.

## Where to start

| Package | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `viveeditor` | One script that turns textareas into editors, with the toolbar. Also exports `mountEditor`, `upgradeTextarea`, `upgradeAll` and everything from the packages it bundles. |
| `@viveeditor/core` | Editor engine and extension system built on ProseMirror: schema, commands, HTML and JSON, paste cleaning. No toolbar. |
| `@viveeditor/ui` | Floating toolbar, selection bubble, `/` menu, panels, File menu and readability meter. |

The `viveeditor` package re-exports `core`, `ui`, `ext-basic`, `ext-code-block`, `ext-embed`, `ext-format`, `ext-image`, `ext-list`, `ext-office-paste`, `ext-search`, `ext-table` and `ext-task-list`. Its CDN build carries the same features.

## Editing features

| Package | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `@viveeditor/ext-basic` | Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, inline code, links, headings, quotes, rules, line breaks |
| `@viveeditor/ext-list` | Bullet and ordered lists |
| `@viveeditor/ext-format` | Text alignment, text colour and highlight |
| `@viveeditor/ext-task-list` | Checklists |
| `@viveeditor/ext-code-block` | Code blocks with a language picker and optional syntax colouring |
| `@viveeditor/ext-table` | Tables with merged cells, header rows and column widths |
| `@viveeditor/ext-search` | Find and replace that handles Turkish capitals |
| `@viveeditor/ext-character-count` | Character count and limit |
| `@viveeditor/ext-image` | Images with checked addresses, safe uploads and alt-text reminders |
| `@viveeditor/ext-embed` | YouTube, Vimeo and Spotify players rebuilt from checked links |
| `@viveeditor/ext-office-paste` | Clean paste from Word, Google Docs and LibreOffice with real lists |

## Extras (npm only)

These are not in the CDN script. Their menus and panels come from `@viveeditor/ui/extras`.

| Package | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `@viveeditor/ext-mention` | `@` mentions with checked ids |
| `@viveeditor/ext-math` | LaTeX formulas drawn by your own KaTeX |
| `@viveeditor/ext-footnote` | Footnotes edited in place, numbered on published pages |
| `@viveeditor/emoji-data` | Compact emoji list for the emoji menu |

Templates and the AI assistant need no extension package; they are UI plugins in `@viveeditor/ui/extras`.

## File converters

| Package | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `@viveeditor/markdown` | Markdown import and export, and Markdown-aware paste |
| `@viveeditor/docx` | Word (`.docx`) import and export with limits for untrusted files |

The File menu receives them as loader functions, so they download only when used.

## Framework components

| Package | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `@viveeditor/react` | React component and `useViveEditor` hook |
| `@viveeditor/vue` | Vue component with `v-model` and `useViveEditor` composable |
| `@viveeditor/svelte` | Svelte component with `bind:value` and a `use:viveEditor` action |
| `@viveeditor/angular` | Angular component for `ngModel` and reactive forms |
| `@viveeditor/element` | `<vive-editor>` form field for any page |

See [Frameworks](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/frameworks/).

## Server packages

| Package | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `@viveeditor/sanitize` | Server-side HTML cleaning for Node that matches the editor output |
| `viveeditor/sanitizer` (PHP) | The same sanitizer for PHP 8.4+, without dependencies |
| `viveeditor/laravel` (PHP) | Blade component, local editor files and `@viveHtml` for Laravel 12+ |

The PHP packages are installed with Composer and versioned separately. See [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/) and [Laravel](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/laravel/).

## Extra entry points

Some packages have more than one entry, so heavy or page-side code stays out of the editor bundle:

- `@viveeditor/ui/extras`: `mentionMenu`, `emojiMenu`, `templateMenu`, `mathTools`, `footnoteTools`, `aiAssistant` and `suggestionMenu`.
- `@viveeditor/ui/panels`: the panel kit, if you want it in your bundle instead of loaded on first open.
- `@viveeditor/ext-code-block/highlight`: `CodeHighlight` and `shikiHighlighter`.
- `@viveeditor/ext-embed/activate`: `activateEmbeds()` for published pages.
- `@viveeditor/ext-math/render`: `renderMath()` for published pages.
- `@viveeditor/ext-footnote/render`: `renderFootnotes()` for published pages.
- `@viveeditor/markdown/paste`: `MarkdownPaste`.
- `@viveeditor/element/define`: registers `<vive-editor>`.
- `@viveeditor/emoji-data/en`: the English emoji list.

Packages that need layout ship a `style.css` export; the list is on [Installation](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/).

## API reports

Each npm package has a folder under [`api/`](https://github.com/mtvrkan/viveeditor/tree/main/api), for example [`api/core`](https://github.com/mtvrkan/viveeditor/tree/main/api/core) or [`api/ui`](https://github.com/mtvrkan/viveeditor/tree/main/api/ui). It holds the published `.d.ts` type declarations. When the public API changes, the change shows up in these files during review, so you can read them to see exactly what a package exports in a given version.

---

# Security and CSP

> How viveEditor keeps unsafe markup out, why you sanitize again on the server, and the CSP settings the CDN script needs.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

viveEditor protects you in two layers: the editor only produces a known set of HTML, and your server cleans every posted document again. This page explains both layers, the Content Security Policy settings the CDN script and its add-ons need, and how to report a vulnerability.

## What the editor checks

The document schema is an allowlist. Markup it does not know never reaches the output. Typed text, pasted HTML, opened files and templates all go through the same rules.

- Links accept only allowed protocols: `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `tel`.
- Every address is checked when content is loaded and again when it is written out, because JSON content skips the HTML parser.
- A `style` attribute only carries values the editor wrote, such as a checked colour or an alignment.
- Images need `https` addresses. `data:` addresses work only with `allowBase64`, and SVG never does. `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:`, `blob:` and `filesystem:` are always refused.
- Video players never keep the address they were given. The editor stores the provider and the video id and rebuilds the player address with a fixed `sandbox`, `allow` and `referrerpolicy`.
- AI answers and mention names are shown and inserted as plain text, never as HTML. A mention id never becomes a link.

## Sanitize again on the server

The browser is not a security boundary. Anyone can post any HTML to your server, so clean it there before you store or show it. `@viveeditor/sanitize` for Node and `viveeditor/sanitizer` for PHP keep exactly what the editor produces and remove everything else.

```ts
import { sanitizeHtml } from '@viveeditor/sanitize'

const clean = sanitizeHtml(request.body.html, { embeds: true })
```

Clean when you save, and print stored HTML through a cleaning helper too, so rows written before you added cleaning stay safe. Options, limits and errors are on [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/).

## Content Security Policy

### The CDN script and its add-ons

The CDN script loads three add-ons on first use from its own folder: `viveeditor.docx.iife.js`, `viveeditor.markdown.iife.js` and `viveeditor.panels.iife.js`. Each one is checked against a `sha384` fingerprint built into the main script.

- `script-src` must allow the folder that holds the scripts, for example `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/viveeditor@x.y.z/dist/` with your exact version.
- If you use a `nonce`, put it on the main script. It is copied to the add-ons.
- With Trusted Types enforced, add the policy name `viveeditor` to the `trusted-types` directive. The policy allows only the add-on addresses.
- If you host the files yourself, keep the file names and serve them with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so the fingerprint check can run.
- The folder is taken from the main script's own address, which must be named `viveeditor.classic.iife.js` and served over `http` or `https`.

```html
<script
  nonce="r4nd0m"
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/viveeditor@x.y.z/dist/viveeditor.classic.iife.js"
></script>
```

Replace `x.y.z` with your exact version, and the nonce with the value your server generates for each response. With npm and a bundler there are no add-ons; the converters and panels load from your own build. The Laravel package serves the editor files from your own `public/vendor/viveeditor`, and its tags get the nonce when you use `Vite::useCspNonce()`.

### Images: `img-src`

Restrict `img-src` to the hosts that serve your uploads and the image hosts you accept. By default, images pasted from other sites keep their original address (`remoteImages: 'allow'`), and showing them tells that site who read the page and when. For a hardened setup use `'drop'` or `'rehost'`; see [Images and uploads](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/images-and-uploads/).

### Video embeds: `frame-src`

List only the providers you enabled:

- YouTube: `https://www.youtube-nocookie.com`
- Vimeo: `https://player.vimeo.com`
- Spotify: `https://open.spotify.com`

A page-wide `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` stops YouTube players from working. On the server, never allow every `iframe`; rebuild players from `div[data-embed]`, or accept only addresses for which `isAllowedEmbedSrc()` returns true. More on [Video embeds](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/video-embeds/).

### Styles: `style-src`

Text colour, highlight, alignment and table column widths are written as `style` attributes, both in the editor and in the saved HTML. A `style-src` without `'unsafe-inline'` makes the browser ignore those attributes, so the colours and widths disappear. Allow `'unsafe-inline'` in `style-src` on pages that show or edit content, and keep `script-src` strict.

### Printing

Printing uses a hidden frame without scripts that loads only images and styles. It is sandboxed without `allow-scripts` and carries its own CSP.

## Uploads

The editor checks every image address and file before it reaches the document, but your upload endpoint must still:

- re-validate and re-encode every upload, which strips EXIF and GPS data and polyglot files, and return the real width and height;
- serve uploads from a cookieless domain with a server-set `Content-Type` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`;
- require authentication, a CSRF token and a rate limit;
- guard against SSRF if it fetches remote images.

## Report a vulnerability

Report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub's "Report a vulnerability" button on the [Security tab](https://github.com/mtvrkan/viveeditor/security) of the repository. Do not open a public issue.

1. Name the affected package and version.
2. Add a minimal reproduction.
3. Describe the impact you observed.

You will receive an acknowledgement, and the fix will be coordinated with you before public disclosure. Until 1.0, only the latest published minor version receives security fixes. The fix ships as a patch release of every package, because all packages share one version number.

Of particular interest is any way to get script execution, event handlers, `javascript:` URLs or unsanitized markup into the editor's output. The server sanitizers are in scope too. The full policy is in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/mtvrkan/viveeditor/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

---

# Accessibility

> How viveEditor meets WCAG 2.2 AA, which keys control it, what screen readers hear, and what you still need to provide.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/accessibility/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

viveEditor targets WCAG 2.2 AA: every tool works from the keyboard, status changes are announced to screen readers, and the editor helps writers describe their images. This page lists what the editor does and the few things you still need to provide, such as a label.

## How it is tested

Every test page, every panel and both themes are checked with axe against WCAG 2.2 AA; a failure blocks the build. The `/` menu and the suggestion lists keep the focus in the text while you pick an option, following the combobox pattern, and a keyboard test proves that every option can be reached.

## Give the editor a name

Screen readers need a name for the editing area. Pass `label` everywhere you create an editor:

```ts
import { mountEditor } from 'viveeditor'

mountEditor(document.querySelector('#editor'), { label: 'Article body' })
```

The components take the same `label` prop, and `<vive-editor>` takes a `label` attribute. With a textarea, keep a visible `<label for>` that points at it; the editor uses that text when you pass no `label`.

Set `locale` too, or a correct `<html lang="...">`, so the toolbar names and messages are read in the page's language. The interface has Turkish and English text.

## Keyboard

| Keys | What they do |
| --- | --- |
| `Alt+F10` | Move the focus from the text to the toolbar |
| `Ctrl+K` | Open the link panel |
| `Ctrl+F` | Open find and replace |
| `/` | Open the block menu |
| `Esc` | Close the selection bubble or a loading panel |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | Change the level of a list item |
| `Tab` | In a table, move to the next cell |
| `Ctrl+Enter` | Tick a checklist item |
| `Ctrl+Shift+L`, `E`, `R`, `J` | Align left, centre, right or justify |
| `Ctrl+J` | Open the AI assistant, when you added it |

On a Mac, use `⌘` where the table says `Ctrl`. Markdown shortcuts also work while typing, such as `## ` for a heading, `- ` for a list or `[ ]` for a checklist. The full list is on [Toolbar and shortcuts](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/toolbar-and-shortcuts/).

## What screen readers hear

- File menu progress is announced through a `role="status"` region, and errors appear in a visible `role="alert"` notice.
- While a panel loads, a placeholder with `role="status"` sits in its place. If it fails, a message with a Try again button replaces it.
- When a form waits for uploads, a notice with `role="status"` says it will send, and the editor is marked `aria-busy`.
- When a required editor is empty on submit, the editor is marked `aria-invalid="true"`, takes the focus and fires a `vive:invalid` event that you can use to show your own message.

## Images and alt text

The image panel asks for alt text, with the hint "Briefly describe the image for people who cannot see it". A writer can also mark an image as decorative.

- In the saved document, `alt: null` means the description is missing and `alt: ''` means the image is decorative.
- The `requireAlt` option of `Image` (`'off'`, `'warn'` or `'block'`) sets how the alt-text reminder behaves.
- The `imagesWithoutAlt` query lists the images that still need a description, for example before you publish.

## Colours and layout

- Light, dark and auto themes are available. In the dark theme, text colours chosen by the writer are lifted on screen so they stay readable; the saved HTML keeps the stored colour.
- On narrow screens, below 560 px, most tools move into the "More tools" menu.
- Pages that show the content should add `img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }` so images fit small screens.

## Readability meter

The interface includes a readability meter that shows words, sentences, average sentence length, reading time and a readability score. The score uses the Ateşman or the Flesch formula; set it with `readability: 'atesman'` or `readability: 'flesch'` in `createUI`, or hide the meter with `readability: false`.

---

# Versioning

> How viveEditor versions its packages before 1.0, what stays compatible, and why the CDN script needs an exact version.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/versioning/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

viveEditor follows semantic versioning with the usual 0.x rule, and all npm packages share one version number. This page explains what may change between versions, what never breaks, and how to pin a version safely.

## The 0.x rule

viveEditor is in 0.x, before its first stable release.

- A breaking change can ship in a minor version, such as 0.1 to 0.2. It is described in that release's notes.
- Patch versions, such as 0.1.0 to 0.1.1, never break.

Read the release notes before you move to a new minor version. Each version is tagged and published as a [GitHub release](https://github.com/mtvrkan/viveeditor/releases).

## One version for every package

All npm packages, `viveeditor` and every `@viveeditor/*` package, are released together with the same version number. Install them at the same version, so the editor, its extensions and your framework component always match.

The PHP packages, `viveeditor/sanitizer` and `viveeditor/laravel`, are versioned separately through Composer.

## Stored content stays readable

HTML and JSON saved by any 0.x version stay readable by every later 0.x version. Stored content never needs a migration when you update.

The canonical storage format is ProseMirror JSON (`editor.getJSON()`); HTML (`editor.getHTML()`) is a rendering format. You can store either.

## The public API is recorded

The public API of each package is recorded as `.d.ts` files in the [`api/` folder](https://github.com/mtvrkan/viveeditor/tree/main/api) of the repository. The build fails when the API changes without an update to these files, so every change to the public API is visible in review. To see what changed between two versions, compare the `api/` folder at their tags.

## Pin the CDN version

Always load the CDN script with an exact version:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/viveeditor@x.y.z/dist/viveeditor.classic.iife.js"></script>
```

Replace `x.y.z` with the exact version you use. The script loads its add-ons from the same folder and checks them against fingerprints built into that exact version, and an add-on is accepted only when its version matches. A short address such as `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/viveeditor` cannot find them. Load `viveeditor.css` from the same version folder.

## Security fixes

Until 1.0, only the latest published minor version receives security fixes. A fix ships as a patch release of every package, because all packages share one version number. Staying on the latest minor is the way to get them. See [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/).

---

# Frequently asked questions

> Short answers about viveEditor's licence, setup, frameworks, safety, Word support, languages, extras and versions.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/faq/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

These are the questions people ask most often before they add viveEditor to a site. Each answer is short; the linked pages have the details.

## Where to read more

- Setup: [Installation](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/installation/) and [Your first editor](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/first-editor/).
- Frameworks and server rendering: [Frameworks](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/frameworks/).
- Safe storage: [Server sanitizing](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/server-sanitizing/) and [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/).
- Images: [Images and uploads](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/images-and-uploads/).
- Word: [Paste from Office](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/paste-from-office/) and [Open, save and print](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/).
- Extras: [Mentions](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/mentions/), [Formulas](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/formulas/) and [AI assistant](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/ai-assistant/).
- Keyboard and screen readers: [Accessibility](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/accessibility/).
- Updates: [Versioning](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/versioning/).
- Something not working: [Troubleshooting](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/troubleshooting/).

If your question is not here, search the [issues on GitHub](https://github.com/mtvrkan/viveeditor/issues) or open a new one. Report security problems privately, as described on [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/).

## Is viveEditor free?

Yes. viveEditor is open source under the MIT licence. Image uploads, tables, embeds and Word import and export are all included; there is no paid tier.

## Do I need a build step?

No. One stylesheet, one script and a textarea with the data-editor attribute are enough. If you use a bundler, install the viveeditor package from npm instead.

## Which frameworks are supported?

There are components for React 18 and 19, Vue 3.5, Svelte 5 and Angular 21 and 22. The vive-editor custom element works as a form field on any other page.

## Can I store the HTML the editor sends as it is?

No. The editor only produces a known set of HTML, but anyone can post any HTML to your server. Clean it there with @viveeditor/sanitize for Node or viveeditor/sanitizer for PHP before you store or show it.

## Can writers upload images?

Yes, once you give the Image extension your own upload function. The editor checks every file and address, but your server must still re-validate and re-encode each upload.

## Does it work with Word?

Yes. Paste from Word, Google Docs and LibreOffice keeps real nested lists, and the File menu opens and saves .docx files. The older .doc, .odt and .rtf formats are not supported.

## Which languages does the interface speak?

Turkish and English. Choose one with the locale option; without it, the editor follows the page's lang attribute and then the browser language.

## Are mentions, emoji, formulas and the AI assistant in the CDN script?

No. Mentions, emoji, formulas, footnotes, templates and the AI assistant ship as npm packages only and plug into the toolbar through @viveeditor/ui/extras.

## Does viveEditor send my text to an AI service?

No. viveEditor sends nothing anywhere itself. The AI assistant calls only the provider function you write, which should call your own server.

## Is it accessible?

viveEditor targets WCAG 2.2 AA, with full keyboard control and screen reader announcements. Every editor still needs a label from you.

## Will an update break my stored content?

No. HTML and JSON saved by any 0.x version stay readable by every later 0.x version. The API itself can still change in a minor version before 1.0.

## Is there a Laravel package?

Yes. viveeditor/laravel works with Laravel 12 or newer and PHP 8.4 or newer. It adds a Blade component, serves the editor files from your own site and includes the PHP sanitizer.

---

# Troubleshooting

> Fixes for common viveEditor problems, from CDN add-ons that fail to load to refused files, blocked players and sanitizer errors.

URL: https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/troubleshooting/
Last updated: 2026-11-01

This page lists the problems people run into most often with viveEditor and what causes them. Find the symptom, check the causes in order, and follow the link if you need the full setup.

## CDN script and add-ons

### Word, Markdown or a panel does not load

The CDN script loads `viveeditor.docx.iife.js`, `viveeditor.markdown.iife.js` and `viveeditor.panels.iife.js` from its own folder on first use. The File menu then says "The converter could not be loaded", or a panel shows "This panel could not be loaded" with a Try again button. Check these causes:

- The script address has no exact version, such as `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/viveeditor`. Use `viveeditor@x.y.z` with your exact version.
- The files were renamed or combined. The main script must keep the name `viveeditor.classic.iife.js`, and the add-ons must sit next to it with their own names.
- You host the files yourself without `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so the fingerprint check cannot run.
- Your Content Security Policy blocks the folder in `script-src`, or Trusted Types is enforced without the `viveeditor` policy name in `trusted-types`.

A failed add-on is removed, so the next use tries again. Loading gives up after 30 seconds. See [Security and CSP](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/security-and-csp/).

### The integrity check fails

Each add-on is checked against a `sha384` fingerprint built into that exact version of the main script, and it is accepted only when its version matches. Load every file from the same version folder, and do not change the files after the build.

### A warning about a second copy

The main script was loaded twice. The second copy warns and passes add-ons it does not own to the first one. Remove the extra `<script>` tag.

### Word and Markdown are missing with npm

With a bundler there are no CDN add-ons. Without loaders, the File menu opens only HTML and text files. Pass the converters in `files`; see [Open, save and print](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/open-save-print/).

## Files and pasted content

### A file is refused

- Word files over 20 MB and text files over 5 MB are refused.
- Password-protected files cannot be opened. Remove the password and try again.
- Word files that unpack too large or too deep are refused with "The file is too large or too complex."
- `.doc`, `.odt` and `.rtf` are not supported. Save the file as `.docx` first.

### Images disappear when a Word file is opened

Opening images from a Word file needs your `upload` function or `allowBase64` in the File menu options. Without one, images are dropped and the menu says how many.

### Images are missing after a paste from Word

Images that point at files on the copying computer cannot be pasted. The `onDropped` callback of `OfficePaste` tells you how many were left out. Insert those images through the image panel.

### An image or link address is refused

- Images need an `https` address. `data:` addresses work only with `allowBase64`, and SVG images never do.
- Links accept `http`, `https`, `mailto` and `tel` only.

## Video embeds

### A link does not turn into a player

- The provider is not in your `providers` list. Built-in providers are YouTube, Vimeo and Spotify.
- The link comes from a link shortener. The editor never follows redirects or short links.
- When you paste, the clipboard must hold the link alone, on an empty line. Otherwise use the video button in the toolbar.
- The document already holds the maximum number of players (`maxEmbeds`, 50 by default).

### Players do not work on the published page

- A page-wide `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` stops YouTube players from working.
- Your `frame-src` does not list the provider.
- You use `facade: true` but do not call `activateEmbeds()` from `@viveeditor/ext-embed/activate` on the page.
- Your server sanitizer removed the players, because `embeds: true` was not passed.

See [Video embeds](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/video-embeds/).

## Extras

### Formulas show their LaTeX source

KaTeX older than 0.18.2 is refused with the error code `KATEX_OUTDATED`, and the source is shown instead. Update KaTeX. If KaTeX fails to load, the code is `KATEX_LOAD`. On published pages, call `renderMath(root, { load: () => import('katex') })` from `@viveeditor/ext-math/render`, and load `katex/dist/katex.min.css`.

### Footnotes are not numbered on the published page

Call `renderFootnotes(root)` from `@viveeditor/ext-footnote/render` on the page that shows the content.

## Server sanitizing

### `TOO_LARGE` or `TOO_COMPLEX`

`sanitizeHtml` throws a `SanitizeError` instead of returning cut or partial output:

- `TOO_LARGE`: the HTML is larger than `maxBytes`, 2 MB by default.
- `TOO_COMPLEX`: the structure would make the parser slow or memory hungry, such as more than 64 attributes on one tag or nesting deeper than 512 levels. The editor never writes such HTML.

```ts
import { SanitizeError, sanitizeHtml } from '@viveeditor/sanitize'

function cleanOrNull(html: string): string | null {
  try {
    return sanitizeHtml(html)
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof SanitizeError) return null
    throw error
  }
}
```

Reject the request when you get `null`.

### PHP ends the request with a fatal error

Some short hostile inputs can reach PHP's `memory_limit` before the check runs. That is safe but not a clean exception. Keep `memory_limit` and `max_execution_time` at their usual values for the endpoints that sanitize, and limit the request body size there.

### A Laravel field reads as an empty string

The `ViveHtml` cast could not clean that row because it is too large or too complex. The error goes to your exception handler. See [Laravel](https://editor.vivepdf.com/en/docs/laravel/).

## Forms and setup

### The form does not submit

- A `required` editor is empty. The textarea fires `vive:invalid` with `detail.reason` set to `'required'`.
- Images are still uploading. The form sends once they finish. If an upload fails while waiting, the send is cancelled and `vive:invalid` fires with `detail.reason` set to `'upload'`.

```ts
document.querySelector('#body').addEventListener('vive:invalid', (event) => {
  console.log((event as CustomEvent).detail.reason)
})
```

### A toolbar button is missing

The toolbar shows only tools whose commands are registered. If you pass your own `extensions`, add the extension for the tool you miss. The File menu is hidden by `data-files="false"` on a textarea or `files: false` in `createUI`.

### `Editor.create` throws a `ViveEditorError`

- `DUPLICATE_EXTENSION`: the same extension is in the list twice.
- `INVALID_SCHEMA`: a dependency is missing, such as the list item for a list.
- `SCHEMA_CONFLICT`: two extensions define the same thing.
- `DESTROYED`: you used the editor after `destroy()`.
- `UNKNOWN_COMMAND`: the command's extension is not loaded.

### The interface is in the wrong language

Pass `locale`. Without it, the editor follows `<html lang="...">` and then the browser language.

### Images are too wide on the published page

Saved images carry their `width` and `height`. Add `img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }` to the pages that show the content.
